<SYSTEM>This is the full developer documentation for Inkbar</SYSTEM>

# Introduction

> What Inkbar does today, what comes next, which packages it ships and where to start.

Inkbar is a PDF viewer and editor for the browser, with form filling, annotations and redaction. It is written in TypeScript, built on PDF.js and released under the MIT licence.

To see it before you install anything, open the [sandbox](https://sandbox.inkbar.dev). It runs the Vue, React, Svelte and plain DOM viewers on a sample document, and you can drop in your own PDF. The file stays in your browser.

## What it does today

| Area              | Available now                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Viewing           | Canvas rendering with a selectable text layer, zoom, pinch zoom on touch screens and trackpads, fit to width or page, continuous or single-page layout, page navigation                                                                                                                                                        |
| Search            | A find bar and Ctrl/Cmd+F in the viewer, and `doc.search` for code. See [Search](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/search/)                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Outline and links | The document’s bookmarks as a tree, links on the page that Tab reaches, and Back and Forward after a jump. See [Outline and links](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/outline-and-links/)                                                                                                                                           |
| Sidebars          | Panels of thumbnails, search results or your own content beside the pages, resizable by drag or keyboard, with widths kept in the [storage](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/) you choose. A rail panel floats over the pages when the document runs out of room. See [Sidebars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/) |
| Forms             | Text, checkbox, radio, choice and signature fields, with the form’s scripts, and `doc.form` for code. See [Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/)                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Signatures        | Draw, type or upload a signature, save it and place it on any page or in a signature field. See [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/)                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Markup            | Highlights, underlines, strikeouts and squiggly underlines from a text selection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Notes             | Notes with reply threads                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Redaction         | Text and area redaction marks. With `@inkbar/engine`, applying them removes the content under them and the file’s metadata, attached files and scripts, then checks the result. See [Redaction](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/redaction/)                                                                                      |
| Drawing           | Freehand ink, shapes, lines, arrows, speech bubbles, loupes, masks and text boxes, with colour and line style menus. See [Drawing](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/drawing/)                                                                                                                                                     |
| Annotations       | JSON export and import, and annotations from other programs shown as locked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| History           | Undo and redo with grouped steps, from the toolbar or Ctrl/Cmd+Z, whether Inkbar or your app holds the annotations. Field edits undo too                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Files             | Download and print the open PDF, from a button or Ctrl/Cmd+S and +P                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Saving            | With `@inkbar/engine`, annotations and form values are written into the PDF, and come back editable when the file is reopened. See [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/)                                                                                                                                             |
| Locked files      | A password dialog for encrypted PDFs, or your own flow. See [Locked files](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/locked-files/)                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Toolbars          | Composable controls for tools, undo and redo, pages and zoom, with icons you can swap for your own                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Keyboard          | Zoom, page and annotation shortcuts, and `Enter` to apply the active tool. See [Tools and keyboard](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#tools-and-keyboard)                                                                                                                                                             |
| Touch             | Pinch to zoom the document, not the page. One finger draws with the drawing tools and two fingers scroll. Plugins can listen for presses and long presses. See [Presses](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/#presses)                                                                                              |
| Translations      | French and German built in, or your own strings for any language. Switch language without a remount. See [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/)                                                                                                                                                           |

You build the toolbars from Inkbar’s controls and place them where they fit your app. There are buttons for the tools, menus for shapes, highlights, signatures, colours, line style and text style, buttons for undo and redo, and previous and next page, plus a page number field, the page count and zoom controls. [Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/) lists them all.

## Not there yet

* **Redacting every kind of content.** Inkbar refuses a mark over patterned fills, some gradients or some soft-masked artwork, since it cannot remove that content from the file. It does not clean hidden layers, and it does not look for the removed words elsewhere in the file, such as in bookmark titles. [Redaction](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/redaction/#limits) lists every limit.
* **XFA forms.** A form built only in XFA shows as a static page.

## Packages

| Package          | Purpose                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@inkbar/core`   | Document model, rendering, annotations and tools, with no framework dependency.    |
| `@inkbar/vue`    | Vue 3 components and composables to build your viewer.                             |
| `@inkbar/react`  | React 19 components and hooks to build your viewer.                                |
| `@inkbar/svelte` | Svelte 5 components and hooks to build your viewer.                                |
| `@inkbar/theme`  | Default stylesheet. Zero specificity, compatible with shadcn token names.          |
| `@inkbar/icons`  | The icons the toolbar controls show, as data, for use on your own buttons.         |
| `@inkbar/engine` | Optional. Writes annotations and form values into the PDF, and applies redactions. |

The packages are released together and share one version number. The framework packages take `@inkbar/core` as a peer dependency, so your app installs one copy of it.

## Where to start

Follow the [Quickstart](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/quickstart/) to put a document on screen with a toolbar.

# Quickstart

> Install Inkbar, add the Vite plugin and put a PDF on screen with a toolbar.

Put a PDF on screen with tools above it and page and zoom controls below. This page assumes a Vite project.

## 1. Install the packages

You need the core, the theme and the package for your framework. The packages share one version number.

* Vue

  ```sh
  pnpm add @inkbar/vue @inkbar/core @inkbar/theme
  ```

* React

  ```sh
  pnpm add @inkbar/react @inkbar/core @inkbar/theme
  ```

* Svelte

  ```sh
  pnpm add @inkbar/svelte @inkbar/core @inkbar/theme
  ```

## 2. Add the Vite plugin

PDF.js loads a worker, fonts and decoders at runtime. The plugin serves those files in development and copies them into your build. It works with Vite 6 or later.

vite.config.ts

```ts
import { inkbar } from '@inkbar/core/vite'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'


export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [inkbar()],
})
```

Note

On another bundler, pass your own asset URLs to the root. [Loading assets](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/loading-assets/) lists the files.

## 3. Mount the viewer

Wrap the viewport in a root. Put a toolbar of tools, undo and redo above it and a page and zoom bar below, then add the popover for notes.

* Vue

  Review\.vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import {
    InkRoot,
    InkViewport,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkToolbarSeparator,
    InkUndo,
    InkRedo,
    InkPrevPage,
    InkPageInput,
    InkPageCount,
    InkNextPage,
    InkZoomSelect,
    InkThreadPopover,
  } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { highlightTool, noteTool, redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
  import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


  defineProps<{ url: string; id: string }>()


  const tools = [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()]
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="{ url, key: id }" :assets="assets" :tools="tools">
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
        <InkToolButton tool="select" />
        <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
        <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
        <InkToolButton tool="note" />
        <InkToolbarSeparator />
        <InkUndo />
        <InkRedo />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
      <InkToolbar label="Page and zoom">
        <InkPrevPage />
        <InkPageInput />
        <InkPageCount />
        <InkNextPage />
        <InkZoomSelect />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkThreadPopover />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  Review\.tsx

  ```tsx
  import {
    InkRoot,
    InkViewport,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkToolbarSeparator,
    InkUndo,
    InkRedo,
    InkPrevPage,
    InkPageInput,
    InkPageCount,
    InkNextPage,
    InkZoomSelect,
    InkThreadPopover,
  } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { highlightTool, noteTool, redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
  import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


  const tools = [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()]


  export function Review({ url, id }: { url: string; id: string }) {
    return (
      <InkRoot src={{ url, key: id }} assets={assets} tools={tools}>
        <InkToolbar>
          <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
          <InkToolButton tool="select" />
          <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
          <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
          <InkToolButton tool="note" />
          <InkToolbarSeparator />
          <InkUndo />
          <InkRedo />
        </InkToolbar>
        <InkViewport />
        <InkToolbar label="Page and zoom">
          <InkPrevPage />
          <InkPageInput />
          <InkPageCount />
          <InkNextPage />
          <InkZoomSelect />
        </InkToolbar>
        <InkThreadPopover />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  Review\.svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import {
      InkRoot,
      InkViewport,
      InkToolbar,
      InkToolButton,
      InkToolbarSeparator,
      InkUndo,
      InkRedo,
      InkPrevPage,
      InkPageInput,
      InkPageCount,
      InkNextPage,
      InkZoomSelect,
      InkThreadPopover,
    } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { highlightTool, noteTool, redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
    import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


    let { url, id }: { url: string; id: string } = $props()


    const tools = [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()]
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={{ url, key: id }} {assets} {tools}>
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
      <InkToolButton tool="select" />
      <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
      <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
      <InkToolButton tool="note" />
      <InkToolbarSeparator />
      <InkUndo />
      <InkRedo />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
    <InkToolbar label="Page and zoom">
      <InkPrevPage />
      <InkPageInput />
      <InkPageCount />
      <InkNextPage />
      <InkZoomSelect />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkThreadPopover />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

`select-text` and `select` are always there. Every other tool is opt-in: pass the ones your toolbar offers as `tools`, from the factories in `@inkbar/core/dom`, so only those end up in your bundle. `allTools()` returns all eight. A button for a tool you did not pass renders disabled and hidden, and logs an `InkError('UnknownTool')` to the console.

The viewer fills its parent, so give the parent a height. Without one, the document has no room to scroll. Each control is its own component: drop the ones you don’t need, move them, or add your own buttons. [Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/) covers them.

Inkbar keeps the annotations itself here, with undo and redo. To hold them in your own state, read [Controlled mode](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/controlled-mode/). Annotations live in memory until you save them. [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/) writes them into the PDF, and [Annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#saving-annotations) shows how to store them as JSON.

## Next

* [Restyle the controls](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/theming/) with your own tokens and CSS.
* [Work with annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/) and save them as JSON.
* [Mark and apply redactions](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/redaction/).
* Read the page for your framework: [Vue](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/vue/), [React](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/react/), [Svelte](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/svelte/) or [Plain DOM](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/).
* Compare with the [sandbox](https://sandbox.inkbar.dev), which runs the same setup in each framework.

# Loading assets

> Serve the PDF.js worker, fonts and decoders with the Vite plugin or from your own server.

PDF.js needs a worker script plus directories of CMaps, standard fonts, WebAssembly decoders and ICC profiles. Inkbar loads them from URLs you pass as the `assets` option. The option has no default, because the right URLs depend on how you deploy your app.

## With Vite

Add the plugin:

vite.config.ts

```ts
import { inkbar } from '@inkbar/core/vite'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'


export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [inkbar()],
})
```

Then import the URLs from the virtual module:

```ts
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
```

In development the plugin serves the files from `node_modules`. In a build it copies them into `<outDir>/inkbar/`. The URLs respect your `base`. With a relative `base` such as `./`, the plugin resolves the URLs at runtime from the location of your bundle, so the build works from any path. Pass `inkbar({ assetsDir: 'pdf' })` to use a different directory name.

For TypeScript, reference the module declaration once, for example in `env.d.ts`:

```ts
/// <reference types="@inkbar/core/vite/client" />
```

## Without Vite

Copy these from the installed `pdfjs-dist` package to a path your server exposes:

* `build/pdf.worker.min.mjs`
* `cmaps/`
* `standard_fonts/`
* `wasm/`
* `iccs/` (optional)

Pass their URLs. Directory URLs end in `/`:

```ts
const assets = {
  worker: '/pdfjs/pdf.worker.min.mjs',
  cMaps: '/pdfjs/cmaps/',
  standardFonts: '/pdfjs/standard_fonts/',
  wasm: '/pdfjs/wasm/',
  icc: '/pdfjs/iccs/',
}
```

Use the `pdfjs-dist` version that `@inkbar/core` depends on, so the worker matches the library.

# Toolbars

> Build toolbars from Inkbar's controls, place them where they fit your app, and swap in your own icons and labels.

Inkbar has no fixed toolbar. You put `InkToolbar` wherever it fits your layout, fill it with the controls you need, and add your own buttons beside them. You can have as many toolbars as you like: the [Quickstart](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/quickstart/) puts the tools above the document and the page and zoom controls below it.

## Controls

| Component                    | What it does                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InkToolbar`                 | Groups its buttons into one Tab stop, with arrow keys between them. `label` names it                                                     |
| `InkToolButton`              | Sets the tool given as `tool`, pressed while that tool is active                                                                         |
| `InkToolbarSeparator`        | Divides groups of controls in a toolbar                                                                                                  |
| `InkToolbarButton`           | Your own button, in the toolbar’s arrow-key order. See [Your own buttons](#your-own-buttons)                                             |
| `InkUndo`, `InkRedo`         | Undo and redo, disabled when there is nothing to undo or redo                                                                            |
| `InkDownloadButton`          | Downloads the open PDF, with the session’s changes when [saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/) is on. `filename` names the file |
| `InkPrintButton`             | Prints the open PDF with the browser’s print dialog                                                                                      |
| `InkApplyRedactions`         | Applies the redaction marks after a confirmation. Needs `engine`. See [Redaction](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/redaction/)              |
| `InkPrevPage`, `InkNextPage` | Previous and next page, disabled on the first and last page                                                                              |
| `InkPageInput`               | The current page number, which the user can type into                                                                                    |
| `InkPageCount`               | “of N”, the page count                                                                                                                   |
| `InkZoomIn`, `InkZoomOut`    | Zoom in or out a step                                                                                                                    |
| `InkZoomSelect`              | Fit width, fit page, and zoom levels from 50% to 400%                                                                                    |
| `InkSearchButton`            | Opens the find bar, pressed while it is open                                                                                             |
| `InkFindBar`                 | The find bar itself. Place it inside `InkRoot`. See [Search](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/search/)                                      |
| `InkHighlightMenu`           | Turns on the `highlight` tool, and picks highlight, underline, strikethrough or squiggly and the markup colour                           |
| `InkShapeMenu`               | Turns on the `shape` tool, and picks the kind. See [Drawing](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/drawing/)                                     |
| `InkLineStyleMenu`           | Line weight, solid or dashed, and arrowheads for the active tool or the selection                                                        |
| `InkColorMenu`               | The `border`, `fill` or `textColor` colour, given as `property`                                                                          |
| `InkTextStyleMenu`           | A text box’s font, size, colour, bold, italic, underline and alignment                                                                   |
| `InkSignatureMenu`           | Sign with the chosen signature, or pick or create one. See [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/)                       |
| `InkCommand`                 | Runs a [plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/plugins/) command given as `id`                                                            |
| `InkIcon`                    | Draws an icon from `@inkbar/icons`, for your own buttons                                                                                 |

`tool` is `select-text`, `select`, or one of the creation tools you pass to the root (see [Choosing tools](#choosing-tools)). The first two are named Select text and Rectangle select. Pass `label` to change a tool button’s name. It takes a string or a function, so the name can follow your language; see [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/#labels-you-supply). To rename any other button, pass `aria-label` and `title`.

Put the controls inside an `InkToolbar`, anywhere inside `InkRoot`. Each one reads its state from that root. Undo and redo follow the root’s history. History is on by default; in controlled mode, turn it on with `history`. The page number field and the zoom select keep their own Tab stops.

Ctrl or Cmd with Z undoes, and Ctrl or Cmd with Shift and Z, or Ctrl with Y, redoes. Both work on every platform. The keys do what `InkUndo` and `InkRedo` do, from anywhere inside `InkRoot`, toolbars included. In a text field, a select or editable content, they act on that element instead.

Ctrl or Cmd with P prints the PDF, and Ctrl or Cmd with S downloads it, from anywhere inside `InkRoot` once the document is ready. Outside the viewer the browser keeps them. The download takes the opened file’s name, or the last part of its URL, or `document.pdf`. Printing opens the browser’s print dialog for the PDF itself, so text stays sharp; on iOS the PDF opens in a new tab, where its own print is. With `@inkbar/engine`, both give the file with this session’s annotations and changed form values written into it: see [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/). Without it, both give the file as it was opened.

## Choosing tools

`select-text` and `select` are always there. Every creation tool is opt-in: import its factory from `@inkbar/core/dom` and pass it to `InkRoot` as `tools`. Only the tools you import end up in your bundle.

| Factory            | Tool          | Button name        |
| ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------ |
| `highlightTool()`  | `highlight`   | Highlight          |
| `redactAreaTool()` | `redact-area` | Mark for redaction |
| `sketchTool()`     | `sketch`      | Sketch             |
| `drawTool()`       | `draw`        | Draw               |
| `shapeTool()`      | `shape`       | Shape              |
| `freetextTool()`   | `freetext`    | Text box           |
| `signatureTool()`  | `signature`   | Signature          |
| `noteTool()`       | `note`        | Add note           |

Pass the tools your toolbar offers:

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { highlightTool, noteTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { InkRoot, InkToolbar, InkToolButton, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const tools = [highlightTool(), noteTool()]
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" :tools="tools">
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
        <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
        <InkToolButton tool="note" />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { highlightTool, noteTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { InkRoot, InkToolbar, InkToolButton, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const tools = [highlightTool(), noteTool()]


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    return (
      <InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} tools={tools}>
        <InkToolbar>
          <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
          <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
          <InkToolButton tool="note" />
        </InkToolbar>
        <InkViewport />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { highlightTool, noteTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
    import { InkRoot, InkToolbar, InkToolButton, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    const tools = [highlightTool(), noteTool()]
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} {tools}>
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
      <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
      <InkToolButton tool="note" />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import {
    createToolbar,
    createToolButton,
    createViewer,
    highlightTool,
    noteTool,
  } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, {
    source: file,
    assets,
    tools: [highlightTool(), noteTool()],
  })


  const tools = createToolbar()
  tools.append(
    createToolButton(viewer, 'select-text'),
    createToolButton(viewer, 'highlight'),
    createToolButton(viewer, 'note')
  )
  viewer.element.prepend(tools)
  ```

To offer every tool, pass `allTools()`, which returns a fresh instance of each of the eight:

```ts
import { allTools } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


const tools = allTools()
```

A button for a tool you did not pass renders disabled and hidden. `InkHighlightMenu`, `InkShapeMenu` and `InkSignatureMenu` render nothing without their tool. Each logs an `InkError('UnknownTool')` to the console once. If the active tool leaves `tools`, the viewer switches to `select-text` and reports it through `onToolChange` (`update:tool` in Vue). A [plugin’s](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/plugins/) tools join the viewer’s on their own.

## Your own buttons

`InkToolbarButton` is a button of your own inside an `InkToolbar`. It joins the toolbar’s arrow-key focus and takes the theme’s toolbar button styles. What it shows and does is up to you.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkToolbarButton @click="download">Download</InkToolbarButton>
  ```

  Button attributes such as `aria-label`, and listeners, pass through to the button. It takes `as-child` and `disabled`.

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkToolbarButton onClick={download}>Download</InkToolbarButton>
  ```

  It takes the props of a `<button>`, with `type="button"` by default, and `asChild`.

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkToolbarButton onclick={download}>Download</InkToolbarButton>
  ```

  It takes the attributes of a `<button>` and a `child` snippet.

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  const download = document.createElement('button')
  download.type = 'button'
  download.textContent = 'Download'
  download.onclick = save
  toolbar.append(download)
  ```

  No wrapper is needed. `createToolbar()` gives any `<button>` you append the same arrow-key focus, and the theme styles it like the toolbar’s own buttons.

`InkIcon` (`createIcon` in plain DOM) draws an `@inkbar/icons` icon on such a button, as the next section shows.

## Icons and labels

Every button shows an icon from [`@inkbar/icons`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@inkbar/icons) until you give it your own content. `InkApplyRedactions` is the exception: it shows its name as text. The accessible name stays the same either way. This bar goes inside an `InkRoot` whose `tools` include `redactAreaTool()`.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import {
    InkIcon,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolbarButton,
    InkToolButton,
    InkUndo,
  } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { Eraser } from 'your-icon-library'
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkToolbar label="Review">
      <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" label="Mark">
        <Eraser />
      </InkToolButton>
      <InkUndo />
      <InkToolbarButton aria-label="Finish review" @click="finish">
        <InkIcon :icon="Check" />
      </InkToolbarButton>
    </InkToolbar>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import {
    InkIcon,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolbarButton,
    InkToolButton,
    InkUndo,
  } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { Eraser } from 'your-icon-library'


  export function ReviewBar({ finish }: { finish: () => void }) {
    return (
      <InkToolbar label="Review">
        <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" label="Mark">
          <Eraser />
        </InkToolButton>
        <InkUndo />
        <InkToolbarButton aria-label="Finish review" onClick={finish}>
          <InkIcon icon={Check} />
        </InkToolbarButton>
      </InkToolbar>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
    import {
      InkIcon,
      InkToolbar,
      InkToolbarButton,
      InkToolButton,
      InkUndo,
    } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { Eraser } from 'your-icon-library'


    let { finish }: { finish: () => void } = $props()
  </script>


  <InkToolbar label="Review">
    <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" label="Mark">
      <Eraser />
    </InkToolButton>
    <InkUndo />
    <InkToolbarButton aria-label="Finish review" onclick={finish}>
      <InkIcon icon={Check} />
    </InkToolbarButton>
  </InkToolbar>
  ```

Install `@inkbar/icons` only if you want its icons on your own buttons. The controls bring their own. The [Icons](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/reference/icons/) reference lists them all.

## Rendering your own element

`InkRoot`, `InkToolbar`, `InkToolButton`, `InkToolbarButton`, `InkCommand`, `InkUndo`, `InkRedo`, `InkDownloadButton`, `InkPrintButton`, `InkApplyRedactions`, `InkPrevPage`, `InkNextPage`, `InkZoomIn` and `InkZoomOut` can render your own element in place of theirs, such as a button from your design system. In React, pass `asChild`. In Vue, pass `as-child`. In Svelte, use the `child` snippet and spread the `props` it gives you. The control keeps its behaviour and accessible name.

## Without a framework

`@inkbar/core/dom` has the same controls as functions for a [`createViewer`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#the-whole-viewer) viewer: `createToolbar`, `createToolButton`, `createToolbarSeparator`, `createUndo`, `createRedo`, `createDownloadButton`, `createPrintButton`, `createApplyRedactionsButton`, `createPrevPage`, `createNextPage`, `createPageInput`, `createPageCount`, `createZoomIn`, `createZoomOut`, `createZoomSelect`, `createSearchButton`, `createFindBar`, `createHighlightMenu`, `createShapeMenu`, `createLineStyleMenu`, `createColorMenu`, `createTextStyleMenu`, `createSignatureMenu`, `createCommandButton` and `createIcon`. A `<button>` you append to `createToolbar()` joins its arrow-key order with no wrapper.

## Styling

The theme gives a toolbar a background and padding, and styles the controls in it. You decide where the toolbar sits and what separates it from the document. Set `--ink-control-size` on a toolbar to change the height of its buttons, fields and zoom select (default `2.25rem`), and `--ink-icon-size` to change the size of their icons (default `1.125rem`):

```css
.my-page-bar {
  --ink-control-size: 2rem;
  --ink-icon-size: 1rem;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--border);
}
```

A tool button carries `data-tool` and `data-state="on|off"`, so `[data-tool="highlight"][data-state="on"]` targets the active highlight tool.

# Annotations

> Which annotations Inkbar creates and displays, how to save them, how to follow changes and how the tools work from the keyboard.

Annotations are plain typed objects. Every coordinate is in PDF user space: points, origin bottom-left, before the page’s `/Rotate`. The numbers stay the same at any zoom, rotation or screen size.

## Types

The model knows 16 annotation types. Every one displays, whether it comes from a tool, your own code, a JSON import or the PDF itself.

| Type                                 | Created by                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `highlight`                          | The `highlight` tool                                             |
| `underline`, `strikeout`, `squiggly` | The `highlight` tool, with the kind picked in `InkHighlightMenu` |
| `redact`                             | The `redact-area` tool                                           |
| `text` (a note)                      | The `note` tool                                                  |
| `ink`                                | The `draw` and `sketch` tools, and a drawn signature             |
| `square`, `circle`                   | The `shape` tool’s rectangles and ellipses, and `sketch`         |
| `line`, `polyline`                   | The `shape` tool’s lines and arrows, and `sketch`                |
| `polygon`                            | The `shape` tool’s stars and polygons, and `sketch`              |
| `freetext`                           | The `freetext` tool, and the `shape` tool’s speech bubble        |
| `loupe`, `mask`                      | The `shape` tool                                                 |
| `stamp`                              | The `signature` tool, for a typed or uploaded signature          |

[Drawing](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/drawing/) covers the drawing tools and [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/) the signature tool.

Each annotation has an `id`, a 0-based `page`, a bounding `rect`, a `#RRGGBB` `color` and an `opacity`. Optional fields are `author`, `contents`, `inReplyTo` for note replies, and `custom` for your own data. Inkbar keeps `custom` as it is, except the `inkbar` key, which it writes and reads itself. Keep your own data under a key of your own, such as `custom.myapp`.

## Usage

```ts
import { openDocument } from '@inkbar/core'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets' // from the Vite plugin, see Loading assets


const doc = await openDocument(file, { assets })
await doc.ready


doc.annotations.add({ type: 'highlight', page: 0, quads })
```

`file` can be a `File`, `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer`, `Uint8Array`, a URL string, `{ url, key }` when the URL is signed and changes between loads, or `{ data, key }` for bytes you want to identify. `quads` is a list of quads in PDF user space. `add` fills in the id, colour, timestamps and bounding box.

In a framework app, `useAnnotations()` gives you the same `add`, `update` and `remove` for the nearest `InkRoot`.

## Saving annotations

There are two ways to keep annotations. [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/) writes them into the PDF with `@inkbar/engine`. Or store them as JSON in your own backend, and import them the next time the document opens:

```ts
const data = doc.exportAnnotations('json')
await saveToYourBackend(doc.key, data)


// On the next open
doc.importAnnotations(await loadFromYourBackend(doc.key), { mode: 'replace' })
```

`doc.key` stays the same between opens only when you open with a key: a URL string, `{ url, key }` or `{ data, key }`. A `File`, `Blob` or raw bytes get a new random key each time, so pass `{ data, key }` with your own document id.

The export is a [Gloss](https://gloss-format.org) document, `{ format: 'gloss', version: 1, documentKey, annotations }`, and holds the annotations made in the session, not the ones embedded in the file. Gloss is an open JSON format for PDF annotations, and its [JSON Schema](https://gloss-format.org/schema/v1.json) lets your backend validate what it stores. The [Gloss format](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/reference/gloss/) reference covers what Inkbar adds to Gloss and what it leaves out.

`importAnnotations` takes the object or a JSON string. `replace` drops the current session annotations first. `merge` overwrites by id and keeps the rest. Items with a type this version does not know come back in the result’s `unknown` list, and the next export writes them out again.

In a framework app, `useDocument()` returns `exportAnnotations()` and `importAnnotations()` for the open document. In controlled mode your app already holds the list, so you can save that directly.

## Annotations from the PDF

Annotations already in the file are drawn by PDF.js on the page canvas. Inkbar adds them to the list with `source: 'pdf'` and `locked: true`, so people can select and read them, but cannot move, resize or delete them. `hasAppearance` says whether the file carries its own appearance for one. PDF.js draws a note only when it does, so Inkbar draws the icon of a note without one. Exports leave out `source`, `locked` and `hasAppearance`. `doc.embedded`, or `useEmbedded()`, counts them by subtype, including subtypes Inkbar does not model.

Annotations that Inkbar itself saved into the file are the exception. They come back as session annotations with their original ids, ready to edit, and `doc.embedded` stops counting them. [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/#opening-a-saved-file) covers when they arrive and which ones stay locked.

## Annotation changes

`doc.annotations.on('change', fn)`, and `onChange(next, change)` in controlled mode, describe each mutation:

* `{ kind: 'add', annotation }`
* `{ kind: 'update', id, before, after }`
* `{ kind: 'remove', annotation, removed }`. Removing a note also removes its replies, so `removed` lists everything that went: `annotation` first, then the replies. A host that syncs by change should delete every id in `removed`.
* `{ kind: 'replace', reason }` for an import, a history step or a controlled sync. Read the whole list.

`add` throws if `input.id` is already in the list. Locked annotations refuse changes to their geometry, `page` and `contents`.

## Undo and redo

Inkbar records history when it holds the annotations, and in controlled mode when you turn `history` on. Put `InkUndo` and `InkRedo` in a toolbar to give people the buttons; each disables itself when there is nothing to undo or redo. Ctrl or Cmd with Z undoes, and Ctrl or Cmd with Shift and Z, or Ctrl with Y, redoes.

To drive history from your own UI, `useHistory()` returns `canUndo`, `canRedo`, `undo`, `redo`, `clear` and `batch` for the nearest `InkRoot`. Without a framework, `doc.history` has `undo`, `redo`, `clear` and `batch`, with `canUndo` and `canRedo` as readables, and `createUndo` and `createRedo` build buttons for a `createViewer` viewer.

`history.batch(fn)` records everything `fn` changes as one undo step, so a host that adds many annotations at once can undo them together. Change events still fire once per annotation. `fn` must be synchronous, and nested calls join the outer batch. The default limit is 200 steps. In controlled mode `doc.history` records nothing, so in a framework app call `batch` from `useHistory()`, which works in both modes.

## Tools and keyboard

`createToolController` from `@inkbar/core/dom` routes pointer and key events on the viewport to the active tool. `select-text` and `select` are always there. The creation tools, `highlight`, `redact-area`, `sketch`, `draw`, `shape`, `freetext`, `signature` and `note`, are there when you pass them in `tools`: [Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/#choosing-tools) shows how. Highlights, text redactions, notes, shapes, text boxes and signatures can be made from the keyboard. Area redactions, freehand drawing, loupes and masks need a pointer.

| Where focus is               | Key                                           | Effect                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Viewport, `highlight` tool   | `Enter`                                       | Turns the text selection into a highlight                                                           |
| Viewport, `redact-area` tool | `Enter`                                       | Turns the text selection into text redactions                                                       |
| Viewport, `note` tool        | `Enter`                                       | Places a note at the centre of the current page and focuses it                                      |
| Viewport, `shape` tool       | `Enter`                                       | Places the current kind at the centre of the current page, except a loupe or mask                   |
| Viewport, `freetext` tool    | `Enter`                                       | Places a text box at the centre of the current page and opens it for typing                         |
| Viewport, `signature` tool   | `Enter`                                       | Places the chosen signature at the centre of the current page                                       |
| Viewport                     | `+` or `=`, `-`                               | Zoom in, zoom out                                                                                   |
| Viewport                     | `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`           | First, last, previous, next page                                                                    |
| Anywhere in the viewer       | `Ctrl` or `Cmd` + `Z`                         | Undo                                                                                                |
| Anywhere in the viewer       | `Ctrl` or `Cmd` + `Shift` + `Z`, `Ctrl` + `Y` | Redo                                                                                                |
| Annotation                   | `Enter` or `Space`                            | Selects and activates it                                                                            |
| Annotation                   | `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`                        | Previous or next annotation on the page, in reading order                                           |
| Annotation                   | `Shift` + arrow                               | Moves it 1 pt (`Shift` + `Alt` + arrow: 10 pt)                                                      |
| Annotation                   | `Ctrl` or `Cmd` + `Shift` + arrow             | Resizes an area redaction, text box or shape by 1 pt. Right and Down grow it, Left and Up shrink it |
| Annotation                   | `Delete` or `Backspace`                       | Removes it                                                                                          |
| Annotation                   | `Escape`                                      | Clears the selection                                                                                |

Pinching zooms the document around your fingers: two fingers on a touch screen, a trackpad pinch, or `Ctrl` + scroll wheel. Pages sharpen when the pinch ends. Two fingers also scroll the document, and under a drawing tool they are how you scroll, because one finger draws. The viewport handles pinching itself, and its `pinchZoom` option turns it off.

The framework packages and `createViewer` install all of these. If you build on `createToolController` directly, it and the overlay handle the tool and annotation keys. The zoom and page keys come from `attachViewportKeys`, which the tool controller does not install. Attach it to the same container:

```ts
import { attachViewportKeys } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


const detach = attachViewportKeys(container, {
  viewport,
  pageCount: () => doc.pages.length,
})
// later: detach()
```

On a focused annotation, `Enter` or `Space` selects it and calls `onActivate`. In the framework packages, a note or text markup opens its thread.

Locked annotations, such as those embedded in the file, ignore move, resize and delete. Without a text selection, `Enter` in the `highlight` and `redact-area` tools does nothing.

`redact-area` draws an area mark when you drag. To redact text instead, select the text with the `select-text` tool, switch to `redact-area`, then click inside the selection or press `Enter`. The tool keeps the press from starting a new text selection, so it cannot select text itself.

With either select tool, or on what a `shape` or `freetext` tool just made, a selected area redaction, text box, shape or drawing shows four corner handles (`.ink-handle[data-handle="nw|ne|sw|se"]`), and a line shows one at each end (`data-handle="start|end"`). Dragging a corner resizes it, and `Shift` keeps its aspect ratio; the store records a single update on release. Drag the annotation itself to move it. Drag a box over empty space to select several annotations, and hold `Shift` to add to the selection.

# Drawing

> Draw freehand, add shapes, lines and text boxes, and set their colour, line style and text style from the toolbar or from code.

Four tools draw on the page:

| Tool       | Button label | Makes                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sketch`   | Sketch       | Freehand ink. A stroke that looks like a shape becomes that shape                                          |
| `draw`     | Draw         | Freehand ink. Strokes made in quick succession join one drawing                                            |
| `shape`    | Shape        | Lines, arrows, rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, speech bubbles, stars, polygons, loupes and masks |
| `freetext` | Text box     | Text boxes                                                                                                 |

Everything they make is an ordinary annotation, so it exports, imports and undoes like the rest. [Annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#types) lists which type each one becomes.

Each one is opt-in. Pass the ones you offer as `tools`, from `sketchTool()`, `drawTool()`, `shapeTool()` and `freetextTool()` in `@inkbar/core/dom`.

## A drawing toolbar

`InkShapeMenu` is a split button for the `shape` tool: the main button draws the current kind, and the arrow opens a grid of kinds. Next to the tools, three menus style what you draw and what you select:

* `InkLineStyleMenu` sets the line weight, solid or dashed, and arrowheads.
* `InkColorMenu` sets one colour. `property` picks which: `border`, `fill` or `textColor`.
* `InkTextStyleMenu` sets a text box’s font, size, colour, bold, italic, underline and alignment.

- Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import {
    InkColorMenu,
    InkLineStyleMenu,
    InkRoot,
    InkShapeMenu,
    InkTextStyleMenu,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolbarSeparator,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { drawTool, freetextTool, shapeTool, sketchTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const tools = [sketchTool(), drawTool(), shapeTool(), freetextTool()]
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" :tools="tools">
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="select" />
        <InkToolButton tool="sketch" />
        <InkToolButton tool="draw" />
        <InkShapeMenu />
        <InkToolButton tool="freetext" />
        <InkToolbarSeparator />
        <InkLineStyleMenu />
        <InkColorMenu property="border" />
        <InkColorMenu property="fill" />
        <InkTextStyleMenu />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

- React

  ```tsx
  import {
    InkColorMenu,
    InkLineStyleMenu,
    InkRoot,
    InkShapeMenu,
    InkTextStyleMenu,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolbarSeparator,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { drawTool, freetextTool, shapeTool, sketchTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const tools = [sketchTool(), drawTool(), shapeTool(), freetextTool()]


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    return (
      <InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} tools={tools}>
        <InkToolbar>
          <InkToolButton tool="select" />
          <InkToolButton tool="sketch" />
          <InkToolButton tool="draw" />
          <InkShapeMenu />
          <InkToolButton tool="freetext" />
          <InkToolbarSeparator />
          <InkLineStyleMenu />
          <InkColorMenu property="border" />
          <InkColorMenu property="fill" />
          <InkTextStyleMenu />
        </InkToolbar>
        <InkViewport />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

- Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import {
      InkColorMenu,
      InkLineStyleMenu,
      InkRoot,
      InkShapeMenu,
      InkTextStyleMenu,
      InkToolbar,
      InkToolbarSeparator,
      InkToolButton,
      InkViewport,
    } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { drawTool, freetextTool, shapeTool, sketchTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    const tools = [sketchTool(), drawTool(), shapeTool(), freetextTool()]
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} {tools}>
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="select" />
      <InkToolButton tool="sketch" />
      <InkToolButton tool="draw" />
      <InkShapeMenu />
      <InkToolButton tool="freetext" />
      <InkToolbarSeparator />
      <InkLineStyleMenu />
      <InkColorMenu property="border" />
      <InkColorMenu property="fill" />
      <InkTextStyleMenu />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

- Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import {
    createColorMenu,
    createLineStyleMenu,
    createShapeMenu,
    createTextStyleMenu,
    createToolbar,
    createToolbarSeparator,
    createToolButton,
    createViewer,
    drawTool,
    freetextTool,
    shapeTool,
    sketchTool,
  } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, {
    source: file,
    assets,
    tools: [sketchTool(), drawTool(), shapeTool(), freetextTool()],
  })


  const tools = createToolbar()
  tools.append(
    createToolButton(viewer, 'select'),
    createToolButton(viewer, 'sketch'),
    createToolButton(viewer, 'draw'),
    createShapeMenu(viewer),
    createToolButton(viewer, 'freetext'),
    createToolbarSeparator(),
    createLineStyleMenu(viewer),
    createColorMenu(viewer, { property: 'border' }),
    createColorMenu(viewer, { property: 'fill' }),
    createTextStyleMenu(viewer)
  )
  viewer.element.prepend(tools)
  ```

A style menu disables itself while neither the active tool nor the selection has that property. When a selection mixes values, the menu shows it as mixed.

## Freehand

`draw` turns each press, drag and release into a stroke. A stroke that starts within a second of the last one joins the same drawing, so a handwritten word stays one annotation. Each stroke is still its own undo step. Switching tools or pressing `Escape` ends the drawing. Pens record pressure, and the stroke thins where you press lightly. A mouse records none. With `draw`, `sketch`, shapes, area redaction and text boxes, one finger draws and two fingers scroll and zoom. A finger tap draws nothing, while a pen tap or mouse click makes a dot. A pen that lands while a palm rests on the screen takes over and draws. A shape, area redaction or text box gives one-finger scrolling back once it has made something.

`sketch` draws each stroke as its own annotation and tidies it. If a stroke looks like a line, an arrow, a rectangle, an ellipse, a polygon or a star, it becomes that shape, styled as shapes are. A click, or a stroke under 4 CSS px across, stays ink. One undo turns the shape back into your stroke, and a second removes it. Draw each shape in one stroke: for an arrow, draw the shaft and then the head without lifting.

The recogniser is exported for your own input. `recogniseStroke(points)` from `@inkbar/core` takes points in PDF user space and returns the shape it found with a score from 0 to 1, or `undefined`. `sketch` swaps in the shape at `RECOGNISE_THRESHOLD` (0.8) or above.

## Shapes

With the `shape` tool, drag to draw the current kind between the press and the release, or click to place one 72 pt across. `Enter` in the viewport places one at the centre of the current page. Hold `Shift` while you drag for a square or circle, or to snap a line to the nearest 45 degrees.

A speech bubble is a text box with a tail. Inkbar stores it as a PDF free-text callout, so other viewers show a box with a leader line.

Stars start with 5 points and polygons with 6 sides. Set the kind, `points` or `sides` through the tool’s options. In a framework app, `useToolOptions('shape')` returns the options and `setOptions`. With `createViewer`, call `set` or `setOptions` on `viewer.tools.get()`:

```ts
viewer.tools.get()?.set('shape', { kind: 'star', points: 7 })
```

### Loupes and masks

A loupe is a circle that shows the page under its centre at twice the size. A drag sizes it, and a click places one 72 pt across. It magnifies the page, not the annotations on it, and its rim takes the shape colour and line weight.

A mask dims the page outside a rectangle (Mask) or an ellipse (Oval mask) by half. Inside it, the page works as usual: you can select text, highlight it and add notes. A page has one mask, so adding a second replaces the first in the same undo step. The style menus have nothing to change on a mask.

Loupes and masks need a pointer. `Enter` does not place them.

## Text boxes

With the `freetext` tool, click to place a text box with its top-left corner at the press, or drag to size one. `Enter` places one at the centre of the current page. The box opens for typing at once, and joins the annotations, selected, once it has text.

Text boxes offer the PDF standard families: Helvetica, Times and Courier. Pass `fonts` to `InkRoot` or `createViewer` to offer your own. A PDF writer has to embed any font beyond the standard three.

## After you draw

`sketch` and `draw` stay on until you pick another tool. `shape` and `freetext` make one thing each and select it, so you can drag it or its handles straight away. A press on empty page, or `Escape`, then clears the selection and switches back to `select-text`. Press another annotation to select it instead.

A selected shape, text box or drawing shows four corner handles. Drag one to resize, and hold `Shift` to keep the aspect ratio. A line has a handle at each end that moves that end alone. A speech bubble’s corner handles resize its box, and its tip handle moves the tip. Each drag is one undo step. The [keyboard table](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#tools-and-keyboard) covers moving and resizing without a pointer.

## Style

Each tool draws in the style of its group, and the groups are shared between tools:

| Group    | Used by                                                                                                               |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shape`  | Lines, arrows, rectangles, ellipses, stars, polygons, loupes, a speech bubble’s outline and the shapes `sketch` makes |
| `ink`    | `draw` and `sketch` strokes                                                                                           |
| `text`   | Text boxes and a speech bubble’s text                                                                                 |
| `markup` | Highlights, underlines, strikeouts and squiggly underlines                                                            |
| `redact` | Redaction marks                                                                                                       |

Changing a colour with a shape tool on changes it for the next line and the next rectangle too. Until you set a style, each type takes the theme’s default. With something selected, the menus show and change the selection’s style. The change is one undo step.

The line style menu offers weights from 0.5 to 8 pt, solid or dashed, and arrowheads at either end. Each colour menu offers a palette plus Custom, which opens the browser’s colour picker. The fill menu also has No fill. Pass `group` to an `InkColorMenu` to tie it to one group whatever tool is on, as `InkHighlightMenu` does for the markup colour.

To read or set the style from code, use `useToolStyle()` in a framework app. Without a framework, use `viewer.engine.get()?.toolStyle`. `current` holds the values the menus show, with `'mixed'` where a selection disagrees, and `set` takes the same props the menus write:

```ts
const style = useToolStyle()


style.set({ border: '#1D4ED8', width: 2, dashes: null })
style.set({ fontSize: 14, fontWeight: 'bold' }, { group: 'text' })
```

Colours are `#RRGGBB`. `fill: null` means no fill and `dashes: null` means a solid line. The tool style belongs to the open document: opening another starts again from the theme’s defaults.

# Search

> Find text with the find bar or from code, read where each match sits on the page, and turn matches into a plugin's records.

Inkbar searches the page text. Your users get a find bar that floats over the pages, and your code gets `doc.search`, which returns each match with its place on the page. The bar runs on `doc.search` too, so the bar and your code find the same matches for the same query.

## The find bar

`InkSearchButton` opens the bar, and `InkFindBar` is the bar itself. Put the button in a toolbar. Put the bar anywhere inside `InkRoot`: it moves itself into the viewport, and the theme floats it over the top-right of the pages. It stays hidden until it opens.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import {
    InkFindBar,
    InkRoot,
    InkSearchButton,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { highlightTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const tools = [highlightTool()]
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" :tools="tools">
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
        <InkSearchButton />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
      <InkFindBar />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import {
    InkFindBar,
    InkRoot,
    InkSearchButton,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { highlightTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const tools = [highlightTool()]


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    return (
      <InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} tools={tools}>
        <InkToolbar>
          <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
          <InkSearchButton />
        </InkToolbar>
        <InkViewport />
        <InkFindBar />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import {
      InkFindBar,
      InkRoot,
      InkSearchButton,
      InkToolbar,
      InkToolButton,
      InkViewport,
    } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { highlightTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    const tools = [highlightTool()]
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} {tools}>
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
      <InkSearchButton />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
    <InkFindBar />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import {
    createFindBar,
    createSearchButton,
    createToolbar,
    createToolButton,
    createViewer,
    highlightTool,
  } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, { source: file, assets, tools: [highlightTool()] })


  const tools = createToolbar()
  tools.append(createToolButton(viewer, 'highlight'), createSearchButton(viewer))
  viewer.element.prepend(tools)


  viewer.element.querySelector('[data-ink-viewport-root]')!.append(createFindBar(viewer))
  ```

  In plain DOM the bar does not move itself. Append it to `[data-ink-viewport-root]` so the theme can float it.

The bar has a field, the match count, previous and next buttons, a match-case toggle and a close button. As the user types, Inkbar starts searching from the current page, highlights every match and scrolls to the first one it finds.

* **Enter** steps to the next match and **Shift+Enter** to the previous. Both wrap around at the ends of the document.
* **Escape** or the close button hides the bar, clears the highlights and sends focus back to where it was before the bar opened.
* **Ctrl+F** (**Cmd+F** on a Mac) opens the bar, but only while focus is inside the viewer and a bar is mounted. Text selected on the page, up to 200 characters, becomes the query. Anywhere else on your page, the browser’s own find keeps the key.
* The count reads “3 of 17”, with a trailing “…” while pages remain to scan, or “No results”. A live region tells screen reader users the match number and page as they step.
* Pressing the search button while the bar is open moves focus back to the field.

The bar has no whole-word or regular expression toggles. `doc.search` takes both, [below](#searching-from-code).

`InkSearchButton` takes `asChild` (`as-child` in Vue, the `child` snippet in Svelte), like the other toolbar controls. In React and Svelte, the bar handles Escape and stops it, so an `onKeyDown` (`onkeydown` in Svelte) you pass to `InkFindBar` never sees that key.

## Your own control

`useSearch()` returns the state behind the find bar and the actions that change it. In plain DOM the same object is `viewer.search`, and plugins get it as `ctx.search`.

| State       | What it holds                                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `open`      | Whether the search is open                                         |
| `query`     | The query                                                          |
| `matchCase` | Whether case must match                                            |
| `hits`      | The matches found so far, as [search hits](#search-hits), in order |
| `current`   | The index of the current hit in `hits`, or -1 when there is none   |
| `scanning`  | Whether pages remain to scan                                       |

| Action             | What it does                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open(query?)`     | Opens the search, with a new query if you pass one                              |
| `setQuery(query)`  | Sets the query and searches again                                               |
| `setMatchCase(on)` | Turns match case on or off and searches again                                   |
| `next()`           | Moves to the next hit and scrolls to it                                         |
| `previous()`       | Moves to the previous hit and scrolls to it                                     |
| `select(index)`    | Makes hit `index` current and scrolls to it. An index out of range does nothing |
| `close()`          | Closes the search and clears the hits. It keeps the query and toggle            |

`open()` searches and draws the highlights even with no find bar on the page, so you can build your own. In Vue `state` is a ref, in React a plain value, and in Svelte a getter, so read it through the returned object. In plain DOM `viewer.search.state` is a readable. Before `InkRoot` mounts, and during server rendering, the state reads closed and the actions do nothing.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { useSearch } from '@inkbar/vue'


  const search = useSearch()
  </script>


  <template>
    <button type="button" @click="search.open('invoice')">Find invoices</button>
    <span>{{ search.state.value.hits.length }} found</span>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { useSearch } from '@inkbar/react'


  export function FindInvoices() {
    const search = useSearch()
    return (
      <>
        <button type="button" onClick={() => search.open('invoice')}>
          Find invoices
        </button>
        <span>{search.state.hits.length} found</span>
      </>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { useSearch } from '@inkbar/svelte'


    const search = useSearch()
  </script>


  <button type="button" onclick={() => search.open('invoice')}>Find invoices</button>
  <span>{search.state.hits.length} found</span>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  button.addEventListener('click', () => viewer.search.open('invoice'))
  viewer.search.state.subscribe((s) => (count.textContent = `${s.hits.length} found`))
  ```

Call `useSearch` inside `InkRoot`.

## Searching from code

`doc.search(query, options)` finds a string or a regular expression in the open document. Iterate the result with `for await` to get hits as Inkbar scans each page, or call `all()` to wait for the whole list:

```ts
for await (const hit of doc.search('invoice')) {
  console.log(hit.page, `${hit.before}[${hit.text}]${hit.after}`)
}


// UK National Insurance numbers
const ni = await doc.search(/\b[A-Z]{2}\d{6}[A-D]\b/).all()
```

A string matches the text as a reader sees it. It ignores case, accents, ligatures and curly quotes, and it finds words split across a line break or a hyphen at the end of a line. A regular expression runs on that same text.

| Option      | What it does                                                                                   |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `matchCase` | Case must match. Default `false`. A regular expression ignores it and follows its own `i` flag |
| `wholeWord` | A hit must not have a letter, digit or underscore on either side. Default `false`              |
| `pages`     | The page indices to search, from 0, in the order you give. Default: every page, first to last  |
| `signal`    | An `AbortSignal`. Aborting it stops the scan, which then throws the signal’s reason            |

The scan yields to the browser between pages, so a long document keeps the page responsive. To stop a search the user no longer wants, abort it:

```ts
const controller = new AbortController()
cancelButton.onclick = () => controller.abort()


try {
  const hits = await doc.search('total', { signal: controller.signal }).all()
} catch (error) {
  if (!controller.signal.aborted) throw error
}
```

Closing the document stops a running scan too, with an `AbortError`. Plugin commands receive a `signal` that aborts when the document closes, so pass it straight through.

## Search hits

| Field             | What it holds                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `page`            | The page index, from 0                                                   |
| `start`, `end`    | Offsets into `doc.pageText(page)`                                        |
| `text`            | The page text the hit covers                                             |
| `quads`           | One quad for each run of text the hit touches, in PDF user space         |
| `rect`            | The box around `quads`                                                   |
| `exact`           | Whether every quad follows the page’s own glyph positions                |
| `before`, `after` | Up to 40 characters of page text on each side, with whitespace collapsed |

Each quad follows where the page draws each glyph, and spans the font’s full height, so it covers ascenders and descenders. You can pass `quads` straight to a text markup annotation, such as a highlight or a redaction mark.

`exact` is `false` when Inkbar could not match some of the text to the page’s glyphs. Right-to-left and vertical text cause this, as do some unusual files. Inkbar then cuts that quad at estimated widths, which can fall short of the glyphs. Pad those quads before you use them to cover text, as you would for a redaction.

`page` and `start` together identify a hit. The same query on the same document gives the same pair, so use them as a key, for example as a record id.

## In a plugin

Inkbar has no “redact all” or “highlight all” button. Actions on every match belong in a plugin. This one adds a command that finds National Insurance numbers, keeps each as a record, and draws a mark over it:

```ts
import type { Quad, RecordBase, Rect } from '@inkbar/core'
import { definePlugin } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


interface NiNumber extends RecordBase {
  page: number
  quads: Quad[]
  rect: Rect
  text: string
}


const NI_NUMBER = /\b[A-Z]{2}\d{6}[A-D]\b/


export const niNumbers = definePlugin('ni-numbers', (plugin) => {
  const found = plugin.records<NiNumber>('found')


  plugin.command('find', 'Find NI numbers', async ({ doc, signal }) => {
    const hits = await doc.search(NI_NUMBER, { signal }).all()
    const added = found.in(doc).addMissing(
      hits.map((hit) => ({
        id: `${hit.page}:${hit.start}`,
        page: hit.page,
        quads: hit.quads,
        rect: hit.rect,
        text: hit.text,
      }))
    )
    return added.length === 1 ? '1 new match' : `${added.length} new matches`
  })


  plugin
    .marks(found, {
      rect: (n) => n.rect,
      label: (n) => `NI number ${n.text}`,
      className: 'ni-mark',
    })
    .scrollToFirst()
})
```

The `(page, start)` key makes `addMissing` skip a number the plugin already holds, so running the command twice adds nothing new. Place the command with `<InkCommand id="ni-numbers.find" />`. To turn a record into a redaction mark the user can undo, link the records to `redact` annotations with `found.annotates`, as [Writing a plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/#linked-annotations) shows.

The `plugin` that `setup` receives also carries the viewer’s search as `plugin.search`, the same object as `useSearch()`, for a plugin that opens the find bar or reads its hits.

## Theming

`@inkbar/theme` colours the matches with two tokens:

| Variable               | Used for        |
| ---------------------- | --------------- |
| `--ink-search-hit`     | Every match     |
| `--ink-search-current` | The current one |

The theme declares them on `[data-ink-root]`, so set yours there:

```css
[data-ink-root] {
  --ink-search-hit: #fff3b0;
  --ink-search-current: #ffd84a;
}
```

The theme draws the matches in a layer that multiplies with the page, so the text stays dark on top of the colour and the matches sit under the annotations. Pages stay white in dark mode, so one pair of colours serves both themes.

# Sidebars

> Put panels beside the pages, fill them with thumbnails, search results or your own markup, and list a plugin's records as cards.

A sidebar holds panels. Each panel shows content you give it: a list of page thumbnails, search results, the cards of a plugin’s records, or markup of your own. Inkbar places nothing for you. Put a sidebar on either side of the viewport with your own flex or grid layout.

## A sidebar of panels

Each panel has an `id`, a `label` (a string, or a function that returns one, see [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/#labels-you-supply)), an optional `icon` (an `IconNode` from `@inkbar/icons`) and an optional `badge`, a number or short string that stays hidden when it is empty or 0.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { MessageSquare, Square } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { InkPanel, InkRoot, InkSidebar, InkThumbnails, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
  import { ref } from 'vue'


  import MyNotes from './MyNotes.vue'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const open = ref<string | null>('pages')
  const noteCount = ref(3)
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets">
      <div class="app">
        <InkSidebar side="left" layout="rail" v-model:open="open">
          <InkPanel id="pages" label="Pages" :icon="Square">
            <InkThumbnails />
          </InkPanel>
          <InkPanel id="notes" label="Notes" :icon="MessageSquare" :badge="noteCount">
            <MyNotes />
          </InkPanel>
        </InkSidebar>
        <InkViewport />
      </div>
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { MessageSquare, Square } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { InkPanel, InkRoot, InkSidebar, InkThumbnails, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
  import { useState } from 'react'


  import { MyNotes } from './MyNotes'


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    const [open, setOpen] = useState<string | null>('pages')
    const noteCount = 3


    return (
      <InkRoot src={file} assets={assets}>
        <div className="app">
          <InkSidebar side="left" layout="rail" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
            <InkPanel id="pages" label="Pages" icon={Square}>
              <InkThumbnails />
            </InkPanel>
            <InkPanel id="notes" label="Notes" icon={MessageSquare} badge={noteCount}>
              <MyNotes />
            </InkPanel>
          </InkSidebar>
          <InkViewport />
        </div>
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { MessageSquare, Square } from '@inkbar/icons'
    import {
      InkPanel,
      InkRoot,
      InkSidebar,
      InkThumbnails,
      InkViewport,
    } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    import MyNotes from './MyNotes.svelte'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    let open = $state<string | null>('pages')
    const noteCount = 3
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets}>
    <div class="app">
      <InkSidebar side="left" layout="rail" bind:open>
        <InkPanel id="pages" label="Pages" icon={Square}>
          <InkThumbnails />
        </InkPanel>
        <InkPanel id="notes" label="Notes" icon={MessageSquare} badge={noteCount}>
          <MyNotes />
        </InkPanel>
      </InkSidebar>
      <InkViewport />
    </div>
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createSidebar, createThumbnails, createViewer } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { MessageSquare, Square } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, { source: file, assets })


  const { element, controller } = createSidebar({
    layout: 'rail',
    side: 'left',
    panels: [
      { id: 'pages', label: 'Pages', icon: Square },
      { id: 'notes', label: 'Notes', icon: MessageSquare, badge: 3 },
    ],
    content: { pages: createThumbnails(viewer), notes: notesElement },
    onOpenChange: (open) => console.log(open),
  })
  shell.prepend(element)
  ```

  `createSidebar` needs no viewer, so it works anywhere you can append an element. Call `controller.destroy()` when you remove the sidebar.

In the framework packages, panels take their place in the order they appear in your markup, including one added later with a conditional. The sidebar needs no document and works outside `InkRoot`. During server rendering it draws its frame with the open panel showing. Rail and tab buttons appear once it has mounted.

## Layouts

`layout` is one of three:

* `rail` (the default) is a strip of icon buttons on the inner edge, beside the document, with each label as a tooltip. One panel is open at a time, with its label as a title above its content, and pressing the open panel’s button closes it, leaving only the rail.
* `tabs` shows labelled tabs across the top with one panel open.
* `stack` shows every panel as a section with a header button, one under another. Any number can be expanded.

`side` is `left` by default and decides which edge the rail and the border sit on. You can change `layout` at any time, and each panel keeps its content when you do.

A closed panel stays in the page, hidden. Its content keeps its state and scroll position, so a half-typed note is still there when the panel opens again.

## Showing and hiding

`visible` (default `true`) shows or hides the whole sidebar, rail and all. A hidden sidebar keeps its open panel, content and scroll for when it shows again. Your code decides when. A results sidebar can stay out of the way until a search finds something:

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { InkPanel, InkSearchResults, InkSidebar, useSearch } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { Search } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { computed } from 'vue'


  const { state } = useSearch()
  const hasResults = computed(() => state.value.hits.length > 0)
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkSidebar side="right" :visible="hasResults">
      <InkPanel id="results" label="Search results" :icon="Search">
        <InkSearchResults :field="false" />
      </InkPanel>
    </InkSidebar>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  function ResultsSidebar() {
    const hasResults = useSearch().state.hits.length > 0
    return (
      <InkSidebar side="right" visible={hasResults}>
  ```
