  ```tsx
        <InkPanel id="results" label="Search results" icon={Search}>
          <InkSearchResults field={false} />
        </InkPanel>
      </InkSidebar>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { InkPanel, InkSearchResults, InkSidebar, useSearch } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { Search } from '@inkbar/icons'


    const search = useSearch()
    const hasResults = $derived(search.state.hits.length > 0)
  </script>


  <InkSidebar side="right" visible={hasResults}>
    <InkPanel id="results" label="Search results" icon={Search}>
      <InkSearchResults field={false} />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  const hasResults = () => viewer.search.state.get().hits.length > 0
  const results = createSidebar({
    side: 'right',
    visible: hasResults(),
    panels: [{ id: 'results', label: 'Search results', icon: Search }],
    content: { results: createSearchResults(viewer, { field: false }) },
  })
  viewer.search.state.subscribe(() => results.controller.update({ visible: hasResults() }))
  ```

`useSearch` needs `InkRoot`, so in the framework packages the sidebar goes in a component of its own inside the root.

## Open and closed

`open` is the id of the open panel (or `null`) for rail and tabs, and the list of expanded ids for stack. Left out, the sidebar starts with its first panel open and keeps its own state. Pass `null` to collapse a tabs sidebar, from a toolbar button of your own for instance.

Pass it and you control the sidebar: a click reports the new value and nothing changes until you set it. The prop to use is `v-model:open` in Vue, `open` with `onOpenChange` in React (or `defaultOpen` to set only where it starts), `bind:open` in Svelte, and `open` with `onOpenChange` and `controller.update({ open })` in plain DOM. When the open panel goes away, rail and tabs open the first one left and stack drops it, and you get the new value the same way.

## Keyboard

Rail and tabs follow the tabs pattern. The sidebar is one Tab stop. On a rail the Up and Down arrows move between buttons, and in tabs the Left and Right arrows do. Home and End go to the first and last, and Enter or Space opens a panel.

Stack headers follow the accordion pattern. Each header is its own Tab stop with `aria-expanded`. Up and Down move between headers, and Enter or Space expands or collapses a section.

## Width

Every sidebar has a resize handle on its inner edge, beside the document. Drag it with a mouse, pen or finger. From the keyboard, Tab to it and use Left and Right to move it 16px at a time, Home for the narrowest and End for the widest. The arrows follow the edge, so on a right-hand sidebar Left makes it wider. Enter or a double-click puts the default width back. The handle hides while no panel is open. Screen readers hear it as “Resize left sidebar” or “Resize right sidebar”; pass `handleLabel` (`handle-label` in Vue) to name it yourself. Like a panel’s `label`, it takes a string or a function.

A sidebar starts 320px wide and stays between 240px and 480px. Change the numbers with `defaultWidth`, `minWidth` and `maxWidth`.

### When there’s no room

Sidebars that share a parent element make room for the document together. While they sit beside it, the document keeps at least 480px. When it would get narrower, because the window shrank, a sidebar opened or someone dragged a handle, a rail sidebar’s panel floats over the pages instead, like a drawer. Its rail stays in place, so the buttons that close and reopen the panel never move. When there’s room again, the panel goes back beside the document.

With two rail sidebars open, the one being resized floats first, then the one opened most recently. Tabs and stack sidebars never float: they narrow toward `minWidth` so the document keeps its room. Floating never changes the width: the saved width, and the one you hear about, stay the width the reader chose.

A floating panel closes the way a drawer does:

* A tap or click on the pages closes it, and does nothing else. No tool draws, no link opens and no field takes focus.
* `Escape` closes it, unless a menu, popover or editor has used the key first.
* Opening the find bar closes it, so the panel never hides the bar.

A scroll, swipe or pinch on the pages leaves it open. When it closes, focus goes back to the rail button, unless the reader was typing somewhere else. A controlled sidebar only reports the close; it stays open until you set `open`.

A sidebar with no room when it first mounts starts with its panel closed, so a phone doesn’t open every document under a drawer. That only applies when you haven’t set `open` or `defaultOpen`. On the server, sidebars render beside the document; floating and starting closed are decided in the browser.

Set the document’s minimum width with `minDocumentWidth`, in CSS pixels. Pass it to the root for every sidebar inside it, or to one sidebar, whose own wins:

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkRoot :src="src" :assets="assets" :min-document-width="600">
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkRoot src={src} assets={assets} minDocumentWidth={600}>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkRoot {src} {assets} minDocumentWidth={600}>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  const { element, controller } = createSidebar({ minDocumentWidth: 600, panels, content })
  ```

The sidebar reads it once, when it is created.

### Keeping the width

Inside the root, a sidebar saves its width in the root’s [`storage`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/) under `sidebar.<name>.width`, so it comes back on the next visit when the store keeps it. `name` defaults to the side, so give two sidebars on one side different names. A sidebar outside the root, or one that should use another store, takes its own `storage`. The sidebar reads `storage` and `name` once, when it is created.

### Controlling the width

To hold the width yourself, bind it the way you bind `open`: `v-model:width` in Vue, `width` with `onWidthChange` in React, `bind:width` in Svelte, and `width` with `onWidthChange` and `controller.update({ width })` in plain DOM. The handle then only reports the new width, and the sidebar neither reads nor saves it.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkSidebar name="tools" side="right" :default-width="360" v-model:width="toolsWidth">
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkSidebar
    name="tools"
    side="right"
    defaultWidth={360}
    width={toolsWidth}
    onWidthChange={setToolsWidth}
  >
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkSidebar name="tools" side="right" defaultWidth={360} bind:width={toolsWidth}>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  const { element, controller } = createSidebar({
    side: 'right',
    name: 'tools',
    storage,
    defaultWidth: 360,
    panels,
    content,
  })
  ```

In Vue and React, a width that starts `undefined` takes control after the first drag and stops saving. Svelte can’t tell an unbound `width` from one bound to `undefined`, so there the sidebar keeps saving until you bind a number.

During server rendering the sidebar draws at its default width with the handle in place. A saved width applies once it mounts.

### In CSS

The sidebar sets `--ink-sidebar-width` on itself, so a CSS override of that variable no longer changes it. Pass `defaultWidth` instead. The rail’s width is still yours to set in CSS with `--ink-sidebar-rail-width` (48px by default). While someone drags the handle, the sidebar has `data-resizing`. A floating sidebar has `data-overlay`: `@inkbar/theme` gives its panel a shadow and puts it above the pages, below menus, popovers and dialogs. Restyle it with `.ink-sidebar[data-overlay] .ink-sidebar-panels`.

## Lists of records

`InkRecordList` (`createRecordList` in plain DOM) lists a plugin’s records as cards. They are the cards the records’ marks open, with the same actions. Name the records `<plugin>.<name>`, as [Writing a plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/#records) names them. The list fills its parent’s height and scrolls, so put it in a panel.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkPanel id="suggestions" label="Suggestions" :icon="MessageSquare" :badge="count">
    <InkRecordList records="review.suggestions" @update:count="count = $event">
      <template #empty>No suggestions left.</template>
    </InkRecordList>
  </InkPanel>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkPanel id="suggestions" label="Suggestions" icon={MessageSquare} badge={count}>
    <InkRecordList
      records="review.suggestions"
      onCountChange={setCount}
      empty="No suggestions left."
    />
  </InkPanel>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    let count = $state(0)
  </script>


  <InkPanel id="suggestions" label="Suggestions" icon={MessageSquare} badge={count}>
    <InkRecordList records="review.suggestions" bind:count>
      {#snippet empty()}No suggestions left.{/snippet}
    </InkRecordList>
  </InkPanel>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createRecordList } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


  panel.append(createRecordList(viewer, { records: 'review.suggestions' }))
  ```

Each record takes its card from the first `plugin.marks` call over those records whose `where` it passes, and the list shows only the records that pass one. When no `marks` call exists for those records, every record is listed, titled with its id and with no actions. A mark with no `card` titles its record with the mark’s label. To choose for yourself, pass `where`, `card` or `sort`. Actions on a card you pass run in one undo step too. The default order is by page, then top to bottom and left to right by the mark’s box.

A new function rebuilds the list, so define `card`, `where` and `sort` once, outside the template or component. In React, wrap them in `useCallback`.

### Selection

The list and the marks share one selection for each set of records, so every list over the same records agrees with the marks.

* Clicking a card, or pressing Enter on it, selects the record, marks its mark with `data-selected` and scrolls the viewer to it. Focus stays in the list and no popover opens.
* Activating a mark selects its card and scrolls every list over those records to it, without moving the page. A list in a closed panel scrolls when it shows.
* Escape in the list clears the selection. So does removing the record or undoing it away.

The list is one Tab stop. Arrow keys move between cards, and Home and End go to the first and last. When the focused card goes, after an action or an undo for instance, focus moves to the next card, then the previous one, then the list. A polite live region says “3 items” when an action or your app adds or removes cards. It stays quiet on undo and redo. An empty list reads “Nothing here yet.”

The count is ready for a panel badge: `@update:count` in Vue, `onCountChange` in React and `bind:count` in Svelte.

### Search results

`InkSearchResults` (`createSearchResults` in plain DOM) is the same list over the viewer’s search: one card for each match, titled with its page (“Page 2”), with its place on the page (“Match 3”) and the text around it. Choosing a card makes its match the current one, as next and previous in the find bar do.

It has its own field, labelled “Find in document”, above the cards, and the find bar’s match count in a footer below them. Before a search it reads “Search to list every match.” The field and the [find bar](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/search/) share one search state, so they never disagree. When a find bar is on the page, leave the field out: `:field="false"` in Vue, `field={false}` in React and Svelte, `{ field: false }` in plain DOM. Unlike other lists, Escape in the results does not clear the current match.

### Your own list

To read and write a plugin’s records from your own component, use `useRecords<T>(name)`. It returns the live `records` and a `handle` to read and write them, and each write is one undo step. `useRecordSelection(name)` returns `selected` and `select(id | null)`. `select` does nothing for an id that has no mark. Both need `InkRoot`. Plugins are set up once the root has mounted, so until then `handle` is null, `records` is empty and nothing is selected.

What the values look like depends on the framework. In Vue, `records`, `handle` and `selected` are refs. In React they are plain values. In Svelte the hooks return an object with getters, so keep the object and read `suggestions.records` or `selection.selected`. Destructuring a Svelte hook loses reactivity.

In plain DOM, `viewer.records<T>(key)` gives the same handle for a key such as `review.suggestions`. Its `list` emits as the records change.

```ts
const suggestions = viewer.records<Suggestion>('review.suggestions')
suggestions.list.subscribe((items) => render(items))
suggestions.batch(() => {
  suggestions.update('s1', { status: 'accepted' })
  suggestions.remove('s2')
})
```

To list something that is not a record set, build a source with `recordsSource` or `searchSource` from `@inkbar/core/dom`, or write one of your own. In the framework packages, pass it as `source` in place of `records`; in plain DOM use `createRecordListController(source)`. It gets the same cards, keys and selection. `card`, `where` and `sort` do not apply to a `source`. With both `source` and `records` given, `source` wins and a development build warns.

To render your own cards, pass a source to `createRecordListController(source)`. Its `rows` give each item, its card and whether it is selected, and `count` and `announcement` give the count and the live-region text. Render each row as an element with `data-ink-record` set to the item’s id, call `attach(element)` on the element holding them, and call `act(id, label)` from each action button. `choose(id)` selects and reveals an item from code. Call `destroy()` when you are done.

## Theming

`@inkbar/theme` styles the list with `.ink-records`, `.ink-record-list`, `.ink-record` and `.ink-record-list-empty`. The selected card has `aria-current="true"`, so style that to change how selection looks. The cards use the same `.ink-card-*` classes as the cards that marks open.

# Thumbnails

> Draw pages as small images, list them as a page navigator, and use one thumbnail in a dialog or a card.

A thumbnail draws one page of the open document as a small image, with its annotations and plugin marks on top. `InkThumbnails` lists them all as a page navigator. Put either anywhere: in a [sidebar](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/) panel, a dialog or a card.

## A list of pages

`InkThumbnails` (`createThumbnails` in plain DOM) lists the pages as thumbnails. Each is a button that scrolls the viewport to its page. It fills its parent’s height and scrolls, so put it in a sidebar panel or any box with a height.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkSidebar>
    <InkPanel id="pages" label="Pages" :icon="Square">
      <InkThumbnails />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkSidebar>
    <InkPanel id="pages" label="Pages" icon={Square}>
      <InkThumbnails />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkSidebar>
    <InkPanel id="pages" label="Pages" icon={Square}>
      <InkThumbnails />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createThumbnails } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


  panel.append(createThumbnails(viewer))
  ```

The thumbnails fill the list’s width, less a 16px gutter on each side, and resize with it, so the space around each page stays even at any panel width. Pass `width` to fix them at that many pixels instead.

`pages` lists only those pages, in that order, from 0: `:pages="[0, 3, 7]"` in Vue, `pages={[0, 3, 7]}` in React and Svelte. Without it every page is listed. A page that does not exist and a repeat are dropped. `annotations` and `marks` work as they do for one thumbnail.

The current page has `aria-current="page"` and scrolls into view in the list when it changes, unless you scrolled the list by hand in the last second. The list is one Tab stop. Arrow keys move between pages, Home and End go to the first and last, and Enter or Space opens one.

Only the items near the visible part of the list are in the document, so a 500-page file stays cheap. When the list scrolls away from the focused item, focus moves to the first visible one without scrolling back.

### Adding to each item

You can add your own content to each item, after its page number. A page count, a status dot or a “reviewed” tick would go here.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkThumbnails>
    <template #item="{ page, current }">
      <span class="page-count">{{ counts[page] }}</span>
    </template>
  </InkThumbnails>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkThumbnails
    renderItem={({ page }) => <span className="page-count">{counts[page]}</span>}
  />
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkThumbnails>
    {#snippet item({ page, current })}
      <span class="page-count">{counts[page]}</span>
    {/snippet}
  </InkThumbnails>
  ```

An item’s height is worked out from its page alone, so position what you add absolutely. It renders inside the item’s `<button>`, so keep it non-interactive: no links, buttons or inputs. Plain DOM has no item slot. To render your own items, build the list on `createThumbnailsController` instead, as [below](#your-own-items).

## One thumbnail

`InkThumbnail` (`createThumbnail` in plain DOM) draws a single page. A page picker in a dialog lets the user tick pages, with a thumbnail inside each checkbox label:

* Vue

  ```vue
  <ul>
    <li v-for="page in pages" :key="page">
      <label>
        <input type="checkbox" :value="page" />
        <InkThumbnail :page="page" :width="96" />
        <span aria-hidden="true">{{ page + 1 }}</span>
      </label>
    </li>
  </ul>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <ul>
    {pages.map((page) => (
      <li key={page}>
        <label>
          <input type="checkbox" value={page} />
          <InkThumbnail page={page} width={96} />
          <span aria-hidden="true">{page + 1}</span>
        </label>
      </li>
    ))}
  </ul>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <ul>
    {#each pages as page (page)}
      <li>
        <label>
          <input type="checkbox" value={page} />
          <InkThumbnail {page} width={96} />
          <span aria-hidden="true">{page + 1}</span>
        </label>
      </li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createThumbnail } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


  const label = document.createElement('label')
  const box = document.createElement('input')
  box.type = 'checkbox'
  box.value = String(page)
  label.append(box, createThumbnail(viewer, { page, width: 96 }))
  ```

| Option        | What it does                                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `page`        | The page, from 0                                                             |
| `width`       | The width in CSS pixels. The height follows the page’s shape                 |
| `height`      | The height in CSS pixels. The width follows. `width` wins when you give both |
| `annotations` | `false` leaves the annotations out. Default `true`                           |
| `marks`       | `false` leaves plugin marks out. Default `true`                              |
| `label`       | Replaces the accessible name. Default “Page 4” for page 3                    |

With neither `width` nor `height`, a thumbnail is 120px wide. It follows the page’s own `/Rotate`, and the viewer’s rotation does not apply.

A thumbnail is an image to assistive technology (`role="img"`). It has no focus and no click behaviour, so wrap it in a button or link when you need one. It renders once it comes within 200px of the visible area, and it shows a placeholder of the right size before then and while no document is open. Form fields show the values saved in the PDF. Annotations follow edits, undo and redo. Marks are drawn with the plugin’s class and style but take no presses.

Both components need `InkRoot` and render empty on the server.

## Your own items

To paint a thumbnail into an element of your own, call `createThumbnailPainter(element, { document, pluginHost }, options)` with readables of the document and, for marks, the plugin host. It adds the `ink-thumbnail` class, its role, name, size and layers, and leaves the element’s own classes and children alone. `update(options)` applies new options, and `destroy()` removes everything it added. `thumbnailSize(pageInfo, { width, height })` gives the size and zoom a thumbnail of that page gets.

To render the whole list yourself, use `createThumbnailsController({ document, pluginHost, viewport }, options)`. Its `state` gives:

* `pages`, the pages listed
* `current`, the current page, or -1 with no viewport
* `window`, the range of indexes into `pages` to mount
* `offsets`, the distance of each item from the top of the list. The last entry is the total height
* `width`, the width each thumbnail is drawn at: your `width` option, or the width that fits the list

Render a spacer of the total height, and each item in the window at its offset. Each item is a button with `data-ink-thumbnail-item` set to its page and a painter inside, wrapped in an element with `itemAttrs(index)` spread on it. That gives it the `listitem` role, plus `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset`, which you need because only the window is mounted. An item is as tall as its thumbnail plus 38px for its label and padding, as the theme draws it.

Call `attach(scrollElement)` once the list is in the document. It follows scrolling, handles clicks and keys, and sets each item’s `tabindex`. `activate(page)` scrolls the viewer to a page.

## Lifetimes

`createThumbnail`, `createThumbnails`, `createRecordList` and `createSearchResults` follow the viewer and stop when it is destroyed, not when you remove their element. For a short-lived use, such as a dialog or a popover, call `createThumbnailPainter` or `createRecordListController` and its `destroy()` when you close it. The framework components clean up when they unmount.

# Outline and links

> Show the document's bookmarks as a tree, follow links on the page, handle web addresses in your app and add Back and Forward buttons.

`InkOutline` lists the document’s bookmarks as a tree. Links in the PDF work on the page with no setup. Following a link or an outline item records where you were, and `InkBack` and `InkForward` move through those positions. Try it in the [sandbox](https://sandbox.inkbar.dev/#/react/outline).

## An outline in a panel

`InkOutline` (`createOutline` in plain DOM) fills its parent’s height and scrolls, so put it in a [sidebar](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/) panel or any box with a height.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkSidebar>
    <InkPanel id="outline" label="Outline" :icon="List">
      <InkOutline empty-text="No sections" />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkSidebar>
    <InkPanel id="outline" label="Outline" icon={List}>
      <InkOutline emptyText="No sections" />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkSidebar>
    <InkPanel id="outline" label="Outline" icon={List}>
      <InkOutline emptyText="No sections" />
    </InkPanel>
  </InkSidebar>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createOutline } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


  panel.append(createOutline(viewer, { emptyText: 'No sections' }))
  ```

A document with no outline shows “This document has no outline”, or your `emptyText`. Both components need `InkRoot` and render empty on the server.

Clicking an item, or pressing Enter on it, goes to its destination without changing the zoom. The chevron expands and collapses an item without following it. Items start expanded or collapsed as the file says, and bold and italic titles keep their style. The file’s colours are ignored. An item Inkbar cannot follow, such as one that points into another file, is greyed out and has `aria-disabled`.

### The current section

The item the reader has reached has `aria-current="location"` and scrolls into view, unless focus is inside the tree. It is the last item whose destination is at or above a line one third of the way down the view. Once the view is scrolled to the end, it is the last item, so the final sections can be reached.

An item you choose stays marked until you scroll away from it. When it sits inside a collapsed parent, the parent is marked instead.

### Keyboard

The tree follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern and is one Tab stop.

* Up and Down move between visible items.
* Right expands an item, then moves to its first child.
* Left collapses an item, then moves to its parent.
* Home and End go to the first and last items.
* `*` expands the item’s siblings.
* Typing jumps to the next title that starts with what you typed.
* Enter follows the item.

### Adding to each item

You can replace an item’s title with your own content. The slot gets the item, whether it is the current one and whether it is expanded.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkOutline>
    <template #item="{ item, current, expanded }">
      <span :class="{ 'is-current': current }">{{ item.title }}</span>
    </template>
  </InkOutline>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkOutline
    renderItem={(item, { current, expanded }) => (
      <span className={current ? 'is-current' : undefined}>{item.title}</span>
    )}
  />
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkOutline>
    {#snippet item(item, { current, expanded })}
      <span class:is-current={current}>{item.title}</span>
    {/snippet}
  </InkOutline>
  ```

Keep what you add non-interactive: no links, buttons or inputs. Plain DOM has no item slot. To render your own tree, build it on `createOutlineController`, as [below](#your-own-tree).

## Links on the page

Links in the PDF work without any setup.

* A click or tap follows a link under the Select text and Rectangle select tools.
* A drag that starts on a link selects text and does not follow it.
* A click with a modifier key held does not follow a link.
* Drawing tools work over links, and a press with one of them does not follow a link.
* Tab reaches each link and each form field in reading order, and Enter follows the focused link. Every link has an accessible name.
* A link Inkbar cannot follow, such as one to another file, does nothing.

### Web addresses

Inkbar never opens a web address on its own. A link or an outline item with a URL calls `onAction` with `{ kind: 'open-url', url, newWindow }`. Only http, https, mailto and tel addresses get that far. Open them in a way that suits your app. This one opens a new tab with `noopener`:

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import type { ViewerAction } from '@inkbar/core'


  function onAction(action: ViewerAction) {
    if (action.kind === 'open-url') window.open(action.url, '_blank', 'noopener')
  }
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" @action="onAction">
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  function onAction(action: ViewerAction) {
    if (action.kind === 'open-url') window.open(action.url, '_blank', 'noopener')
  }


  ;<InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} onAction={onAction}>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import type { ViewerAction } from '@inkbar/core'


    function onaction(action: ViewerAction) {
      if (action.kind === 'open-url') window.open(action.url, '_blank', 'noopener')
    }
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} {onaction}>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  createViewer(el, {
    source: file,
    assets,
    onAction: (action) => {
      if (action.kind === 'open-url') window.open(action.url, '_blank', 'noopener')
    },
  })
  ```

`onAction` also receives the form requests described in [Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/#form-actions).

## Back and Forward

Following a link or an outline item records where you were. `InkBack` and `InkForward` (`createBack` and `createForward` in plain DOM) move through those positions. Each is disabled until there is somewhere to go.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkToolbar>
    <InkBack />
    <InkForward />
  </InkToolbar>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkToolbar>
    <InkBack />
    <InkForward />
  </InkToolbar>
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkToolbar>
    <InkBack />
    <InkForward />
  </InkToolbar>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createBack, createForward } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


  toolbar.append(createBack(viewer), createForward(viewer))
  ```

To render your own buttons, use `as-child` in Vue, `asChild` in React and a `child` snippet in Svelte. In plain DOM, `viewer.back()` and `viewer.forward()` move, and `canGoBack` and `canGoForward` say whether they can.

Scrolling and the page buttons record nothing. The history keeps 50 positions and clears when another document opens. Inkbar adds no keyboard shortcuts for it, so Alt+Left stays the browser’s.

## Your own tree

`doc.outline()` gives the outline as data. Each `OutlineItem` has an `id` (its path, such as `"1.0"`), `title`, `target`, `bold`, `italic`, `open` and `children`. The first call reads it and later calls reuse the result.

To render a tree yourself, use `createOutlineController({ document, viewport, navigation })` with readables of the document, the viewport and the navigation. Spread `treeAttrs()` on the tree (a `ul`) and `itemAttrs(id)` on each item (an `li`). Each item holds a row with `rowAttrs(id)`, which holds the chevron and the title. The title gets `titleAttrs(id)` and names the item. The item’s children follow in a `role="group"` list that shows only while `expanded` has its id.

Pass `onKeydown` to the tree’s keydown, call `activate(id)` on a row click and `toggle(id)` from the chevron, and call `bindScroll(scrollElement)` to keep the current item in view. The controller’s JSDoc has the full markup.

## Theming

`@inkbar/theme` styles the tree with `.ink-outline`, `.ink-outline-item`, `.ink-outline-row`, `.ink-outline-toggle`, `.ink-outline-title` and `.ink-outline-empty`. A row is indented by `--ink-outline-level`, which the markup sets for you. The toggle is a 44px column, so it stays a full touch target. Set these on `[data-ink-root]`:

| Variable                    | Default                  | Used for                               |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `--ink-outline-indent`      | `16px`                   | The indent for each level              |
| `--ink-outline-item-height` | `44px`                   | The minimum height of an item          |
| `--ink-outline-current-bg`  | The accent colour at 10% | The tint behind the current item       |
| `--ink-link-hover`          | `transparent`            | The tint over a link under the pointer |

Links show no box on hover by default, as desktop readers do not. Set `--ink-link-hover` to a translucent colour to add one.

# Forms

> Fill AcroForm fields in the viewer, read and set values from code, handle what a form asks your app to do, and save values as Gloss.

Inkbar fills the AcroForm fields in a PDF: text, checkboxes, radio buttons, combo boxes, lists, push buttons and signature fields. The form’s own scripts run too, so totals calculate and validation works as the author intended.

Values live in memory until a save. With `@inkbar/engine`, Download, Print and `doc.save()` write the changed values into the PDF: see [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/). Without it, store the values yourself: hold them in your own state, or export them as [Gloss](#save-values-as-gloss) and import them the next time the document opens.

## Filling

Fields take input while the default `select-text` tool or the `select` tool is active. Under a drawing or markup tool, a press on a field goes to the tool instead.

A small annotation that sits over a field takes the click when a select tool is active, so select it to move or delete it. Press the part of the field the annotation leaves uncovered to fill it.

Each field has a light tint so people can find it. A focused field gets a ring, and a field whose value was refused gets a red outline. Read-only fields have no tint.

Tab moves through the fields in the order the PDF sets for each page, and carries on to the next page at the last field. Shift+Tab goes back. Enter commits a single-line text field. Space toggles a checkbox, and the arrow keys move between the buttons of a radio group.

A value commits when the field loses focus, when Enter is pressed in single-line text, or at once for a checkbox, radio button, choice or signature. When annotations and fields are both uncontrolled, each commit is one undo step in the same history as annotations, and the calculations it triggers belong to that step.

## Reading and setting values

`doc.form` holds the open document’s form:

```ts
import { openDocument } from '@inkbar/core'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


const doc = await openDocument(file, { assets })


doc.form.fields.get() // each field's name, type, flags, options and widgets
doc.form.values.get() // { 'applicant.name': 'Ada', agree: 'Yes', ... }


const result = doc.form.set({ 'applicant.name': 'Grace', agree: 'Off' })
// { applied: ['applicant.name', 'agree'], rejected: [] }


doc.form.reset() // every field back to the PDF's default
doc.form.reset(['applicant.name'])
```

`fields` and `values` are readables: call `get()` for the current value, or `subscribe()` to follow changes.

Values are keyed by the field’s full name, its name parts joined with dots. A value is one of:

* a string for a text field, a combo box or a single-select list;
* the name of an appearance state for a checkbox or radio group, such as `"Yes"`, or `"Off"` when nothing is checked;
* an array of option values for a multi-select list, in option order;
* `{ signature: id }` for a signed signature field, where `id` is the signature annotation’s id.

`set` commits values as a person would. Each value runs the field’s validate and calculate scripts, and the whole call is one undo step. A value that names no field, targets a read-only field, does not suit the field or is refused by a script stays out, and `rejected` lists it with the reason: `unknown`, `readOnly`, `invalid` or `script`.

`reset` restores the PDF’s default values. Read-only fields reset too. Locked fields keep their values.

In a framework app, `useForm()` returns the same `fields`, `values`, `set` and `reset` for the open document, as reactive state.

## Controlled fields

By default Inkbar holds the values. Pass `fields` to hold them in your own state instead, the way [controlled mode](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/controlled-mode/) works for annotations. Inkbar applies each change at once, then reports the full map along with what changed. Whatever you pass back wins.

The second argument says what changed and names the fields it changed: `commit` (a person, `set` or a signature, plus any fields its calculations changed), `reset`, `import` or `calculate`.

Whether fields are controlled is fixed when a document opens. While you control fields or annotations, Inkbar keeps no undo history. Your app owns undo.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { ref } from 'vue'
  import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import type { FieldValues, ViewerAction } from '@inkbar/core'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const fields = ref<FieldValues>({ 'applicant.name': 'Ada' })


  function onAction(action: ViewerAction) {
    // See "Form actions" below.
  }
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot v-model:fields="fields" :src="file" :assets="assets" @action="onAction">
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

  `update:fields` also carries the change as its second argument. Replace the object to change values yourself: `fields.value = { ...fields.value, agree: 'Yes' }`. In-place changes are not observed.

* React

  ```tsx
  import { useState } from 'react'
  import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/react'
  import type { FieldValues, ViewerAction } from '@inkbar/core'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  export function Application({ file }: { file: File }) {
    const [fields, setFields] = useState<FieldValues>({ 'applicant.name': 'Ada' })


    function onAction(action: ViewerAction) {
      // See "Form actions" below.
    }


    return (
      <InkRoot
        fields={fields}
        onFieldsChange={(next) => setFields(next)}
        onAction={onAction}
        src={file}
        assets={assets}
      >
        <InkViewport />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

  `onFieldsChange` receives the change as its second argument. Set a new object to change values yourself: `setFields({ ...fields, agree: 'Yes' })`.

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import type { FieldValues, ViewerAction } from '@inkbar/core'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    let fields = $state.raw<FieldValues>({ 'applicant.name': 'Ada' })


    function onaction(action: ViewerAction) {
      // See "Form actions" below.
    }
  </script>


  <InkRoot bind:fields src={file} {assets} {onaction}>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

  Pass `onFieldsChange` to hear what changed. Replace the object to change values yourself: `fields = { ...fields, agree: 'Yes' }`.

With `createViewer`, pass a `FieldsMode`. `onChange` hears each change with the full map, and you push values back through `viewer.form`:

```ts
import { createViewer } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
import type { FieldValues } from '@inkbar/core'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


let values: FieldValues = await loadValues()


const viewer = createViewer(el, {
  source: file,
  assets,
  fields: {
    mode: 'controlled',
    initial: values,
    onChange(next) {
      values = next
      saveValues(next)
    },
  },
  onAction: handleAction,
})


// Later, to change a value from your app:
viewer.form.get()?.setControlledValue({ ...values, agree: 'Yes' })
```

`viewer.form.get()` returns `null` until a document is ready. For uncontrolled fields that start from your own values, pass `{ mode: 'uncontrolled', initial }`. Your values apply over the PDF’s.

## Form actions

A form can ask to submit its data, open a link, send mail or print. Inkbar does none of these itself. It turns each request into a `ViewerAction` and hands it to your app. If you do not handle an action, nothing happens.

The handler is `onAction` (`@action` in Vue, `onaction` in Svelte). It also receives links to a web address, as [Outline and links](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/outline-and-links/#web-addresses) shows.

| `kind`     | Fields                                           | Comes from                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `submit`   | `url`, `fields`, `format`, and `method` for HTML | A submit button, or a script’s `submitForm` |
| `open-url` | `url`, `newWindow`                               | A link button, or `app.launchURL`           |
| `mail`     | `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body`, `withData` | `mailDoc` or `mailForm`                     |
| `print`    | none                                             | A print button, or `print()`                |
| `prompt`   | `message`                                        | `app.response`                              |

`submit.fields` holds the values the form wants to send, keyed by full name. It leaves out fields marked no-export and fields with no value. `format` is the format the PDF asked for (`fdf`, `xfdf`, `html` or `pdf`). You can ignore it and send the values in whatever shape your backend expects.

Every URL and mail address is limited to the `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel` schemes. A request with any other scheme, or a relative URL, never reaches your app.

The URL in a `submit` comes from the PDF, so treat it as untrusted. This handler posts the values to your own backend and only opens links after asking:

```ts
import type { ViewerAction } from '@inkbar/core'


async function handleAction(action: ViewerAction) {
  switch (action.kind) {
    case 'submit':
      await fetch('/api/forms', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ fields: action.fields }),
      })
      showToast('Form sent')
      break
    case 'open-url':
      if (confirm(`Open ${action.url}?`)) window.open(action.url, '_blank', 'noopener')
      break
    case 'mail':
      if (action.to) window.location.href = `mailto:${action.to}`
      break
    case 'print':
      window.print()
      break
    case 'prompt':
      // The script has already moved on. Show the question if your app needs the answer.
      break
  }
}
```

To hear actions from code, subscribe on the document’s form. `on` returns a function that stops listening:

```ts
const stop = doc.form.on('action', handleAction)
```

## Scripts

Form scripts run in an isolated sandbox. They can read and set field values, calculate totals, format and validate input, show and hide fields, and move focus. They have no network access, cannot open windows and cannot show browser dialogs.

* `app.alert` shows an Inkbar dialog over the viewer.
* `app.response` cannot wait for an answer. The script gets `null`, and your app gets a `prompt` action.
* Submit, open-URL, mail and print requests become [form actions](#form-actions).

On a document with JavaScript, `ready` waits for the sandbox to load, for up to 10 seconds if the server stalls. Past that, the form opens without scripts.

When a script fails, the form keeps working. The error reaches your error handler (`onError`, or the `error` event in Vue) as a `FormScriptError`. That includes an error raised while the document opens, such as a sandbox that could not start. In code, `doc.form.on('error', fn)` hears it too.

## Signature fields

An empty signature field shows a Sign button. Pressing it opens the signature menu, with the person’s saved signatures and an option to create one. The chosen signature goes inside the field’s box and stays locked to it: it cannot be moved, resized or restyled. To clear the field, select the signature and delete it.

From code, `signField(doc, fieldName, widgetId, template)` from `@inkbar/core` does the same.

Signing is visual only. It places an image or drawing of a signature, and it does not add a digital signature to the file.

## Locked documents

Inkbar honours the locks a PDF sets:

* Fields signed with a certificate are read-only.
* A certifying signature that forbids changes makes the whole form read-only.
* Fields locked by a signature field’s lock list stay as they are.
* Fields the PDF marks read-only cannot be filled, though scripts and `reset` can still change them.

`set` reports a locked or read-only field as `readOnly`.

## Save values as Gloss

`doc.exportAnnotations('json')` adds a `fields` map to the [Gloss](https://gloss-format.org) document when the form has values, and `doc.importAnnotations()` reads it back:

```json
{
  "format": "gloss",
  "version": 1,
  "documentKey": "application-2026.pdf",
  "annotations": [],
  "fields": {
    "applicant.name": "Ada Lovelace",
    "agree": "Yes",
    "newsletter": "Off",
    "topics": ["maths", "engines"],
    "signature": { "signature": "c41f9e" }
  }
}
```

`fields` is a flat map keyed by full dotted name. Each value is a string, an array of strings or `{ signature: id }`, as in `doc.form.values`. Checkbox and radio values are appearance-state names, `"Off"` included. Fields marked no-export are left out.

The import result’s `fields` lists the names it `applied` and the ones it `rejected`, with the same reasons as `set`. An import of field values is not an undo step.

## Not supported

* XFA forms. A PDF with an AcroForm alongside its XFA fills through the AcroForm. A pure XFA form shows as a static page.
* File-select and barcode fields show their appearance but cannot be filled.

## Theming

Three tokens style the fields. Set them on `[data-ink-root]`:

| Variable                   | Used for                       |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `--ink-form-field-bg`      | The tint on fillable fields    |
| `--ink-form-field-focus`   | The focus ring and Sign button |
| `--ink-form-field-invalid` | The outline on a refused value |

To turn the tint off, pass `formHighlight: false` to `createViewer`, or set `formHighlight` to false on `InkRoot`. Changing it later updates the open viewer. With `createViewer`, call `viewer.setFormHighlight(false)`.

# Signatures

> Let people draw, type or upload a signature, keep it for next time, and place it on the page or in a signature field.

A signature in Inkbar is a mark on the page: a drawing, a name typed in a handwriting font, or an image of a scan. Someone creates it once, and Inkbar saves it as a template they can place again on any page. It does not sign the file with a certificate.

## The signature menu

`InkSignatureMenu` is a split button. The main button, Sign, turns on the `signature` tool with the chosen signature, or opens the menu if none is chosen yet. The arrow beside it, Choose signature, lists the saved signatures, each with a remove button, then Create signature, which opens the dialog.

The menu needs `signatureTool()` from `@inkbar/core/dom` in the root’s `tools`. Without it, the menu renders nothing. The signature dialog and signature fields work without it; the dialog then only saves the signature.

Inkbar keeps the templates in the root’s [`storage`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/). Pass a store that lasts, such as `createLocalStorage()`, and `signatureFonts` for the handwriting fonts the dialog offers. Both are optional: without them, signatures last until the page reloads and the dialog offers the browser’s `cursive` font.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { createLocalStorage } from '@inkbar/core'
  import {
    InkRoot,
    InkSignatureMenu,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { signatureTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const tools = [signatureTool()]
  const storage = createLocalStorage('my-app')
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot
      :src="file"
      :assets="assets"
      :tools="tools"
      :storage="storage"
      :signature-fonts="['Dancing Script']"
    >
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="select" />
        <InkSignatureMenu />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { createLocalStorage } from '@inkbar/core'
  import {
    InkRoot,
    InkSignatureMenu,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { signatureTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const tools = [signatureTool()]
  const storage = createLocalStorage('my-app')
  const fonts = ['Dancing Script']


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    return (
      <InkRoot
        src={file}
        assets={assets}
        tools={tools}
        storage={storage}
        signatureFonts={fonts}
      >
        <InkToolbar>
          <InkToolButton tool="select" />
          <InkSignatureMenu />
        </InkToolbar>
        <InkViewport />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { createLocalStorage } from '@inkbar/core'
    import {
      InkRoot,
      InkSignatureMenu,
      InkToolbar,
      InkToolButton,
      InkViewport,
    } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { signatureTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    const tools = [signatureTool()]
    const storage = createLocalStorage('my-app')
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} {tools} {storage} signatureFonts={['Dancing Script']}>
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="select" />
      <InkSignatureMenu />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createLocalStorage } from '@inkbar/core'
  import {
    createSignatureMenu,
    createToolbar,
    createToolButton,
    createViewer,
    signatureTool,
  } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, {
    source: file,
    assets,
    tools: [signatureTool()],
    storage: createLocalStorage('my-app'),
    signatureFonts: ['Dancing Script'],
  })


  const tools = createToolbar()
  tools.append(createToolButton(viewer, 'select'), createSignatureMenu(viewer))
  viewer.element.prepend(tools)
  ```

## Placing a signature

With the `signature` tool on, a click on the page places the chosen signature about 150 pt wide, centred where you pressed. From the keyboard, `Enter` in the viewport places it at the centre of the current page. The new signature is selected, so you can move or resize it straight away, and placing it is one undo step.

A drawn signature becomes an `ink` annotation and the others a `stamp`, both with `subject: 'Signature'`. Both keep their aspect ratio when resized. On a page the PDF rotates with `/Rotate`, the signature still reads upright. Placed signatures export and import with the other annotations.

To place one from code, `placeSignature(template, page, centre)` from `@inkbar/core` returns the annotation to add. `centre` is a point in PDF user space. An optional fourth argument sets the width in points.

```ts
import { placeSignature } from '@inkbar/core'


doc.annotations.add(placeSignature(template, 0, { x: 300, y: 120 }))
```

## Creating a signature

The dialog has three tabs:

* **Draw** has a pad to sign on with a mouse, pen or finger, and a Clear button.
* **Type** takes a name and draws it in one of the `signatureFonts`.
* **Image** takes a PNG or JPEG, such as a scan. Inkbar scales it to at most 1000 px on its long side before storing it.

Save stores the template and makes it the chosen signature. Drawing needs a pointer. The Type and Image tabs work from the keyboard.

To open the dialog from your own button, use `InkSignatureDialog`. Bind `open` the way your framework does (`v-model:open` in Vue, `open` with `onOpenChange` in React, `bind:open` in Svelte). It emits `save` with the new template. Set `select` to false to keep the new signature from becoming the chosen one. Without a framework, `createSignatureDialog(viewer)` returns a dialog with `open`, `close` and `destroy`.

## Fonts for typed signatures

Each entry in `signatureFonts` is a CSS font family name. Inkbar does not load fonts, so load each one with `@font-face` or your font service before you offer it. A menu or dialog can take its own `fonts` list in place of the root’s.

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Dancing Script';
  src: url('/fonts/dancing-script.woff2') format('woff2');
}
```

## Where signatures are kept

Your app owns the templates. Inkbar keeps them as an array in the root’s [`storage`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/) under the key `signatures`, so they go wherever your store puts them:

* With the default memory store they last until the page reloads.
* `createLocalStorage(prefix)` keeps them in `localStorage` under `<prefix>:signatures`. Where the browser blocks storage, it keeps them in memory for the page’s life.
* A [store of your own](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/#writing-your-own) can keep them on your server.

When the store can’t save, the dialog tells the person their signature wasn’t saved. It says browser storage is full only when that’s the reason; a refusal from your server gets a general message. Saves run one at a time, so two quick saves to a slow store both land. Inkbar skips any stored template it can’t read and keeps it on the next write.

A signature belongs to one person, so key the store by user when people share a browser.

### Moving from `createLocalSignatureStore`

0.13.0 removed `createLocalSignatureStore` and the root’s `signatures` option. A template saved by `createLocalSignatureStore('my-app-signatures')` sits under that exact key, so copy it to the new key once if you want people to keep their saved signatures:

```ts
const old = localStorage.getItem('my-app-signatures')
if (old !== null && localStorage.getItem('my-app:signatures') === null) {
  localStorage.setItem('my-app:signatures', old)
  localStorage.removeItem('my-app-signatures')
}
```

### Templates

A template is plain JSON. A drawn one holds its strokes in a unit box, and an image holds a data URL:

```ts
type SignatureTemplate =
  | { id: string; kind: 'ink'; inklist: Point[][]; pressure?: number[][]; aspect: number }
  | { id: string; kind: 'image'; imagedata: string; aspect: number }
```

`aspect` is the width over the height.

## Signature fields

A PDF form’s signature field shows its own Sign button, which opens the same list of saved signatures and the same dialog. The chosen signature goes inside the field and stays locked to it. [Signature fields](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/#signature-fields) in the forms guide has the details.

# Locked files

> Ask for the password of an encrypted PDF with the built-in dialog, replace the panel behind it, or run your own flow.

A PDF can need a password to open. Inkbar asks for it. When a locked file opens, a “Password required” dialog appears, and the reader types the password. There is nothing to set up. Try it in the [sandbox](https://sandbox.inkbar.dev/#/react/locked), where the password is `inkbar`.

## What the reader sees

The dialog has a labelled password field, Open and Cancel.

* A wrong password keeps the dialog open and says “Incorrect password. Try again.”
* Open is disabled while the field is empty and while a try is running.
* Cancel closes the dialog and leaves a panel that says the document is password protected, with an “Enter password” button. The button opens the dialog again.
* Opening another file closes the dialog and starts fresh.

A `password` you pass to the root still applies first. If it is wrong, the dialog opens with the incorrect message already showing.

## The locked status

While the file is locked, the status is `{ state: 'locked', incorrect: boolean }`. `incorrect` is true after a wrong password. The root and viewport carry `data-state="locked"`.

The `error` event, or `onError`, still fires with a `PasswordRequired` error for each failed open, prompt or not.

Inkbar uses the typed password for that one load and for no other file. It does not reach the status, the error, an event or storage. With [`engine`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/), the open document keeps the password until it closes, because a save opens the file again in the engine.

## Turning the prompt off

Pass `passwordPrompt` as `false` to handle locked files yourself. A locked file is then `{ state: 'error', error }`, and `error.code` is `PasswordRequired`.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" :password-prompt="false">
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    return (
      <InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} passwordPrompt={false}>
        <InkViewport />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()
  </script>


  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} passwordPrompt={false}>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { createViewer } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, {
    source: file,
    assets,
    passwordPrompt: false,
  })
  ```

## Replacing the locked panel

The panel behind the dialog is the `locked` part of `InkViewport`. Fill it to show your own. It receives `{ incorrect, promptPassword }`, and `promptPassword` opens the dialog again.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <InkViewport>
    <template #locked="{ incorrect, promptPassword }">
      <p v-if="incorrect">That password did not work.</p>
      <button @click="promptPassword">Unlock this file</button>
    </template>
  </InkViewport>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  <InkViewport
    locked={({ incorrect, promptPassword }) => (
      <>
        {incorrect && <p>That password did not work.</p>}
        <button onClick={promptPassword}>Unlock this file</button>
      </>
    )}
  />
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <InkViewport>
    {#snippet locked({ incorrect, promptPassword })}
      {#if incorrect}<p>That password did not work.</p>{/if}
      <button onclick={promptPassword}>Unlock this file</button>
    {/snippet}
  </InkViewport>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  The plain DOM viewer draws the panel itself, with the classes `ink-status ink-locked`. Style it with the theme, or turn the prompt off and build the flow below.

## Your own flow

To ask for the password your way, turn the prompt off and place the dialog yourself. `InkPasswordDialog` in each framework package and `createPasswordDialog` in `@inkbar/core/dom` are the same dialog the built-in flow uses, with the same markup and theme. It holds no password. Open hands the typed value to your code.

The flow has four steps. A failed open reports `PasswordRequired`, and `error.details.incorrect` is true after a wrong password. Show the dialog with that value. On submit, retry with the typed password and mark the dialog pending. Close the dialog when the document is ready.

* Vue

  `InkRoot` retries when its `password` prop changes. `InkPasswordDialog` takes `v-model:open`, `incorrect` and `pending`, and emits `submit` with the password.

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import type { InkError } from '@inkbar/core'
  import { InkPasswordDialog, InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { ref } from 'vue'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const password = ref<string>()
  const open = ref(false)
  const incorrect = ref(false)
  const pending = ref(false)


  function onError(error: InkError) {
    if (error.code !== 'PasswordRequired') return
    incorrect.value = error.details.incorrect === true
    pending.value = false
    open.value = true
  }


  function onSubmit(typed: string) {
    // The same text as the try that just failed would not reload.
    if (typed === password.value) return
    pending.value = true
    password.value = typed
  }
  </script>


  <template>
    <InkRoot
      :src="file"
      :assets="assets"
      :password="password"
      :password-prompt="false"
      @error="onError"
      @ready="open = false"
    >
      <InkViewport />
      <InkPasswordDialog
        v-model:open="open"
        :incorrect="incorrect"
        :pending="pending"
        @submit="onSubmit"
      />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  `InkRoot` retries when its `password` prop changes. `InkPasswordDialog` takes `open`, `onOpenChange`, `incorrect`, `pending` and `onSubmit`.

  ```tsx
  import type { InkError } from '@inkbar/core'
  import { InkPasswordDialog, InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { useState } from 'react'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    const [password, setPassword] = useState<string>()
    const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
    const [incorrect, setIncorrect] = useState(false)
    const [pending, setPending] = useState(false)


    function onError(error: InkError) {
      if (error.code !== 'PasswordRequired') return
      setIncorrect(error.details.incorrect === true)
      setPending(false)
      setOpen(true)
    }


    return (
      <InkRoot
        src={file}
        assets={assets}
        password={password}
        passwordPrompt={false}
        onError={onError}
        onReady={() => setOpen(false)}
      >
        <InkViewport />
        <InkPasswordDialog
          open={open}
          onOpenChange={setOpen}
          incorrect={incorrect}
          pending={pending}
          onSubmit={(typed) => {
            // The same text as the try that just failed would not reload.
            if (typed === password) return
            setPending(true)
            setPassword(typed)
          }}
        />
      </InkRoot>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  `InkRoot` retries when its `password` option changes. `InkPasswordDialog` takes `open` (bindable), `onOpenChange`, `incorrect`, `pending` and `onSubmit`.

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import type { InkError } from '@inkbar/core'
    import { InkPasswordDialog, InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    let password = $state<string>()
    let open = $state(false)
    let incorrect = $state(false)
    let pending = $state(false)


    function onError(error: InkError) {
      if (error.code !== 'PasswordRequired') return
      incorrect = error.details.incorrect === true
      pending = false
      open = true
    }


    function onSubmit(typed: string) {
      // The same text as the try that just failed would not reload.
      if (typed === password) return
      pending = true
      password = typed
    }
  </script>


  <InkRoot
    src={file}
    {assets}
    {password}
    passwordPrompt={false}
    {onError}
    onReady={() => (open = false)}
  >
    <InkViewport />
    <InkPasswordDialog bind:open {incorrect} {pending} {onSubmit} />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  `createPasswordDialog` takes `onSubmit` and `onCancel`. `open({ incorrect })` shows or updates it, `setPending` disables Open during a try, and `close` and `destroy` end it. `viewer.open(file, { password })` retries with a password for that load only.

  ```ts
  import { createPasswordDialog, createViewer } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  const viewer = createViewer(el, { source: file, assets, passwordPrompt: false })


  const dialog = createPasswordDialog({
    onSubmit: (password) => {
      dialog.setPending(true)
      viewer.open(file, { password })
    },
    onCancel: () => undefined,
  })


  viewer.status.subscribe((s) => {
    if (s.state === 'error' && s.error.code === 'PasswordRequired') {
      dialog.open({ incorrect: s.error.details.incorrect === true })
      dialog.setPending(false)
    } else if (s.state === 'ready') {
      dialog.close()
    }
  })
  ```

# Redaction

> Mark text and areas for redaction, then apply the marks to remove the content under them from the file.

Redaction in Inkbar has two steps. People draw marks over what should go, then apply them. Applying removes the content under the marks, cleans parts of the file, checks the result and opens the redacted file in the viewer.

Caution

A mark on its own removes nothing. The text under it still renders, and anyone can select and copy it. Download, Print and `doc.save()` write a mark into the PDF as a Redact annotation and leave the content under it in the file. Only applying the marks removes that content.

Applying needs `@inkbar/engine`. [Saving](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/#turn-it-on) shows how to install it and pass it as `engine`. Inkbar loads the engine on the first apply, or on the first save that has changes.

## Drawing marks

Pass `redactAreaTool()` from `@inkbar/core/dom` in `tools` to offer the `redact-area` tool. Its tool button is labelled “Mark for redaction”, and it makes two kinds of mark:

* **Area marks.** Drag a box over any part of the page, including images. With the `select` tool you can then move it and resize it by its corner handles, or from the keyboard.
* **Text marks.** Select text with the `select-text` tool, switch to `redact-area`, then click inside the selection or press `Enter`. The mark follows the lines of the selection.

Both are `redact` annotations. `interiorColor` is the colour of the box that replaces the content once the marks are applied. It defaults to `--ink-redact-fill`.

A mark from your own detector is a `redact` annotation too, added through the same API as any other annotation. Anything your review needs, such as a reason or a score, goes in the annotation’s `custom` data.

## Applying marks

The Apply redactions button applies every mark in the session. It is disabled while no document is ready, without `engine`, and while there is no mark.

A press asks first, in a dialog titled “Apply redactions?”. The dialog says:

* how many marks on how many pages will have the content under them removed,
* that this cannot be undone,
* how many other annotations go too, when the marks overlap any,
* that the signature will stop verifying, when the file is signed,
* how many marks saved earlier will be applied too, when an encrypted file holds them.

Focus starts on Cancel. If the marks change while the dialog is open, the viewer asks again about the marks there are now. If every mark has gone by then, nothing is applied. When the document closes or another one opens, the dialog closes and nothing is applied.

While the marks are applied, the button says “Applying redactions…” and keeps focus, and another press does nothing. The document takes no input: the pages take no presses or keys and do not scroll, undo and redo are off, an open comment thread closes, and Download and Print are disabled.

Once the apply succeeds:

* Your `onRedacted` callback (the `redacted` event in Vue) receives `{ bytes, result }`: the redacted file and what was done. A host that stores files stores these bytes.
* The viewer reopens on the redacted file with the same file name, page, zoom, layout, rotation and tool, and the password the file was opened with.
* The marks are gone and undo history starts again.
* Download and Print give the redacted file.
* The message box says how many redactions were applied. It adds a line when the file has hidden layers, and when marks from another program were left in place.

In [controlled mode](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/controlled-mode/), Inkbar proposes your list without the marks it applied and the annotations removed with them, with `reason: 'redaction'`, before the redacted file opens. A mark added while the apply runs stays in that list. With the framework packages’ `history` on, your answer to that proposal starts the history; it is not an undo step.

## What applying removes

The engine works on the file as it was opened:

1. It removes the text, image samples and drawing under each mark, and leaves an opaque box in the mark’s fill colour in its place, with the mark’s overlay text if it has one.
2. It removes every annotation a mark overlaps, Inkbar’s and the file’s own, except masks and other programs’ redaction marks, which stay. Then it writes the other annotations and the changed form values.
3. It removes the file’s metadata, attached files, scripts, page thumbnails and private application data.
4. It rewrites the whole file, so no earlier version stays inside it.
5. It checks the saved bytes under each mark. The check reads the file’s objects, so content hidden under an opaque box counts. When it finds anything, the apply fails and hands nothing over.

Marks Inkbar saved into the file earlier count as marks. In an encrypted file they come back locked, and the engine applies them too. Redact annotations from other programs stay in the file, unapplied, and are counted.

The open document does not change. Its annotations, `doc.changed`, `doc.save()` and `doc.getData()` stay as they were; the viewer shows the redacted file by opening the new bytes.

## Marks the engine refuses

The apply removes text, blanks image samples and cuts paths. A file can also define content once and paint it through a reference, and cutting the shape that paints it would leave that content in the file. So before anything changes, the engine refuses a mark that touches:

* a shape painted with a tiling pattern, such as hatching or a texture,
* a picture gradient: a mesh or function-based gradient, or a linear or radial gradient whose colour function is not a simple ramp,
* artwork under a soft mask that holds more than a simple fade, which is how drop shadows and feathered edges are usually drawn,
* a Type 3 glyph that paints outside the box it declares.

A simple ramp blends from colour to colour in at most eight stretches. A simple fade is a soft mask made of at most four plain rectangles or simple-ramp gradients, which is how gradient transparency is drawn. Content under a simple fade, and linear and radial gradients with a simple ramp, are redacted.

Covering the whole shape does not help. When the engine refuses, nothing is changed, the viewer selects the refused marks, and the message box says how many marks cover content that cannot be removed. Move or delete those marks and apply again. When only marks saved earlier in an encrypted file caused the refusal, the viewer selects nothing and the message says one mark.

## Limits

Read these before you rely on a redacted file:

* Inkbar does not clean hidden layers. `result.hiddenLayers` says when the file has them, and the viewer’s message says so too.
* The removed words may also appear where Inkbar does not look: bookmark titles, comments on other annotations, form values, and alternate text for screen readers.
* Inkbar removes what lies under a mark. It does not find copies of that content elsewhere in the file: a second use of the same graphic that is cropped, covered or on another page, or a pattern or gradient that another page also uses.
* A scanned page is one image. A mark removes the pixels under it, and there is no text to remove. OCR text layers are removed like any text.
* Scripts are removed, so forms stop calculating.
* A signed file’s signature stops verifying.
* The engine refuses a mark over patterned fills, picture gradients, soft-masked artwork that holds more than a simple fade, and out-of-box Type 3 glyphs, even when the mark covers the whole shape.
* An Inkbar loupe that comes back locked, in an encrypted file or after another program edited it, keeps a copy of its page made before the apply. When that page has a mark and no mark overlaps the loupe, the check reads the copy, finds what lay under the mark, and the apply fails. Draw a mark over the loupe as well, and the apply removes it. For a loupe another program edited, you can also delete it in that program. For an encrypted file, you can also save a copy without the password in another program and redact that copy: Inkbar’s loupes come back editable there, unless that program changed them, and the apply rewrites them.
* Text set at an angle close to a mark’s edge can make the check fail, though the apply removed everything under the mark. Move the mark a little further from that text.
* The check also fails, and the reader sees “Some content could not be removed”, for an image that has both a soft mask and a separate stencil mask. It can fail for a very low-quality JPEG.
* A crafted file can make the apply and its check take a long time.

The check after an apply is the engine reading the file it just wrote. It tells you what it found under each mark, within the limits above and those of [`checkRedaction`](#checking-a-file-from-elsewhere). Do not describe a file as safe because the apply succeeded.

## In each front end

`upload` in these examples stands for your own code that stores the redacted bytes.

### Plain DOM

`createApplyRedactionsButton(viewer)` is the button. `viewer.applyRedactions()` runs the same action from code and resolves with `result`, or with `null` when the reader cancelled, nothing was applied or the apply failed.

```ts
import {
  createApplyRedactionsButton,
  createToolbar,
  createToolButton,
  createViewer,
  redactAreaTool,
} from '@inkbar/core/dom'


const viewer = createViewer(el, {
  source,
  assets,
  tools: [redactAreaTool()],
  engine: () => import('@inkbar/engine'),
  onRedacted: ({ bytes }) => upload(bytes),
})


const bar = createToolbar()
bar.append(createToolButton(viewer, 'redact-area'), createApplyRedactionsButton(viewer))
viewer.element.prepend(bar)
```

### Vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
import {
  InkApplyRedactions,
  InkRoot,
  InkToolbar,
  InkToolButton,
  InkViewport,
} from '@inkbar/vue'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


defineProps<{ file: File }>()


const tools = [redactAreaTool()]
const engine = () => import('@inkbar/engine')
</script>


<template>
  <InkRoot
    :src="file"
    :assets="assets"
    :tools="tools"
    :engine="engine"
    @redacted="({ bytes }) => upload(bytes)"
  >
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
      <InkApplyRedactions />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
</template>
```

A `redacted` listener that throws goes to Vue’s own error handling (`app.config.errorHandler` or `onErrorCaptured`), not to the `error` event, and the redacted file still opens.

### React

```tsx
import { redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
import {
  InkApplyRedactions,
  InkRoot,
  InkToolbar,
  InkToolButton,
  InkViewport,
} from '@inkbar/react'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


const tools = [redactAreaTool()]
const engine = () => import('@inkbar/engine')


export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
  return (
    <InkRoot
      src={file}
      assets={assets}
      tools={tools}
      engine={engine}
      onRedacted={({ bytes }) => upload(bytes)}
    >
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
        <InkApplyRedactions />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  )
}
```

### Svelte

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import {
    InkApplyRedactions,
    InkRoot,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkViewport,
  } from '@inkbar/svelte'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


  const tools = [redactAreaTool()]
  const engine = () => import('@inkbar/engine')
</script>


<InkRoot src={file} {assets} {tools} {engine} onRedacted={({ bytes }) => upload(bytes)}>
  <InkToolbar>
    <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
    <InkApplyRedactions />
  </InkToolbar>
  <InkViewport />
</InkRoot>
```

In React and Svelte, when `onRedacted` throws, `onError` hears a `RedactionFailed` error with `details.callback` set to `'onRedacted'`, and the redacted file still opens.

### After the redacted file opens

In Vue, React and Svelte, `InkRoot` shows the redacted bytes in place of `src`, and `src` stays as you passed it. A new `src` opens as usual: a different `key`, or for a source without one, a different URL string, `File` or bytes object. Passing the stored bytes back under the same `key` reopens nothing.

### Your own confirmation

Pass `redactionConfirm` to `createViewer` or `InkRoot` (`redaction-confirm` in Vue) to ask your own way. It receives a preview and resolves `true` to apply. `false` applies without asking.

```ts
const viewer = createViewer(el, {
  source,
  assets,
  tools: [redactAreaTool()],
  engine: () => import('@inkbar/engine'),
  redactionConfirm: async (preview) =>
    window.confirm(
      `Remove the content under ${preview.marks} marks? This cannot be undone.`
    ),
})
```

The preview holds `marks`, `pages`, `overlapped` (the other annotations the marks overlap), `signed` and, in an encrypted file, `lockedMarks`.

### Your own button

`useRedaction()` gives the same action for a control of your own, inside `InkRoot`. `canRedact` and `busy` say when to disable it, and `apply()` resolves with `result`, or with `null` when the reader cancelled, nothing was applied or the apply failed. It never rejects for a failure the viewer has already shown. In Vue `canRedact` and `busy` are refs, in React they are booleans, and in Svelte you read them through the object `useRedaction()` returns.

```tsx
import { useRedaction } from '@inkbar/react'


function RedactButton() {
  const redaction = useRedaction()
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      disabled={!redaction.canRedact || redaction.busy}
      onClick={() => void redaction.apply()}
    >
      Redact
    </button>
  )
}
```

`InkApplyRedactions` also takes your own content and your own element, as the other [toolbar controls](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/#your-own-buttons) do.

### From the document

Without a viewer, `doc.redactionPreview()` gives the counts a confirmation needs without loading the engine, and `doc.applyRedactions()` applies every mark and resolves with `{ bytes, result }`. Open the bytes to show the redacted file.

```ts
const preview = doc.redactionPreview()
if (await ask(preview)) {
  const { bytes, result } = await doc.applyRedactions()
  await upload(bytes)
}
```

An apply never overlaps a save, and a second call while an apply runs gets the same promise.

## What `result` holds

* `marks` and `pages`: the marks applied and the pages they were on. A mark with no area, or wholly off its page, is skipped.
* `removed.session`: the ids of the session annotations removed with the content. `removed.file`: how many of the file’s own annotations went, pop-up windows included.
* `foreignMarks`: other programs’ Redact annotations, left unapplied. `ownLockedMarks`: Inkbar’s earlier marks applied in an encrypted file.
* `fieldsSkipped`: the names of changed form fields that were not written, because a mark removed their widgets.
* `sanitised`: what was removed from the file.
* `hiddenLayers` and `signed`: whether the file has hidden layers, and whether it held a digital signature.
* `findings`: what the check found under each mark. Findings hold places and verdicts, never the file’s text.

## When applying fails

When the apply fails, nothing is handed over and the open document stays as it was. The viewer says why in its message box, and your error handler (`onError`, or the `error` event in Vue) hears one of these errors:

* `EngineUnavailable`: there is no `engine`.

* `NothingToRedact`: there is no mark, or the engine applied none because every mark has no area or lies wholly off its page.

* `RedactionFailed`: the engine could not finish. `details.stage` says where:

  * `'engine'` when the engine could not be loaded or started, as when offline.
  * `'apply'` when the engine refused the marks, or could not apply them or write the rest. `details.page` and `details.annotation` name the page and the annotation when one was the cause.
  * `'verify'` when the check could not run or did not find every mark’s place clean. `details.regions` lists the page and rectangle of each place it did not find clean, and `details.page` names a page the check could not read.

A refusal has `details.reason: 'unremovable-content'`. `details.annotations` lists the ids of every refused mark, `details.annotation` holds the first, `details.kinds` says what was found (`'pattern'`, `'shading'`, `'mask-group'` or `'glyph'`) and `details.page` names the first page. When the engine could not look under the marks, `details.reason` is `'could-not-inspect'`.

The words in the button, the dialog and the message box are in the `viewer` group of messages, from `applyRedactions` to `redactForeign`. [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/) lists them and shows how to change them.
