Change `messages` or `locale` and the viewer relabels in place. It does not remount, reload the document or move the scroll position, and an open menu, popover, dialog or find bar stays open.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { de } from '@inkbar/core/locales/de'
  import { fr } from '@inkbar/core/locales/fr'
  import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/vue'
  import { ref } from 'vue'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  defineProps<{ file: File }>()


  const messages = ref(fr)
  </script>


  <template>
    <button @click="messages = fr">Français</button>
    <button @click="messages = de">Deutsch</button>
    <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" :messages="messages">
      <InkViewport />
    </InkRoot>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { de } from '@inkbar/core/locales/de'
  import { fr } from '@inkbar/core/locales/fr'
  import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/react'
  import { useState } from 'react'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


  export function Viewer({ file }: { file: File }) {
    const [messages, setMessages] = useState(fr)
    return (
      <>
        <button onClick={() => setMessages(fr)}>Français</button>
        <button onClick={() => setMessages(de)}>Deutsch</button>
        <InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} messages={messages}>
          <InkViewport />
        </InkRoot>
      </>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { de } from '@inkbar/core/locales/de'
    import { fr } from '@inkbar/core/locales/fr'
    import { InkRoot, InkViewport } from '@inkbar/svelte'
    import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'


    let { file }: { file: File } = $props()


    let messages = $state(fr)
  </script>


  <button onclick={() => (messages = fr)}>Français</button>
  <button onclick={() => (messages = de)}>Deutsch</button>
  <InkRoot src={file} {assets} {messages}>
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { de } from '@inkbar/core/locales/de'


  viewer.setMessages(de)
  viewer.setLocale('de-CH') // optional
  ```

  `viewer.messages` is a readable of the words and locale in use, as `{ messages, locale }`. `subscribe` calls you after each `setMessages` or `setLocale`. Pieces made without a viewer, such as `createToolbar`, follow it when you pass `messages: viewer.messages`.

## Locale and lang

Each set carries its `lang`: `fr.lang` is `'fr'`. Without a `locale`, the viewer root’s `lang` attribute and the dates on notes follow it, so `messages={fr}` alone reads as French to a screen reader. Pass `locale`, such as `'de-CH'`, when the page language or the date format should differ from the messages.

## Labels you supply

The text you pass in is yours to translate. These each take a string or a function that returns one:

* a tool’s `label`, and the `label` of a toolbar or panel
* a sidebar’s `handleLabel`
* an outline’s `emptyText`
* a plugin command’s label and its `errorStatus`
* a card’s `title`, `label` and action labels

Inkbar calls a function label when it renders and again on every `setMessages` or `setLocale`, so the label follows the language.

```ts
const toolbar = createToolbar({ label: () => t('toolbar'), messages: viewer.messages })


definePlugin('review', (plugin) => {
  const notes = plugin.records<Note>('notes')


  plugin.command('suggest', () => t('suggest'), run, {
    errorStatus: () => t('suggest.failed'),
  })


  plugin.marks(notes, {
    rect: (n) => n.rect,
    label: (n) => t('note.label', { text: n.text }),
    card: (n) => ({
      title: () => t('note.title'),
      actions: [{ label: () => t('note.dismiss'), run: () => notes.remove(n.id) }],
    }),
  })
})
```

A card’s `actions` is an array of `{ label, run }` so each label can be a function. The object form, with the label as the key, works for fixed text. See [Writing a plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/#cards).

## Key reference

Every message in the English set, by group. The table leaves out `lang`, which names the set’s language and isn’t a message. A function message shows its template, or its plural forms, with `{name}` for the values it receives. Your replacement for a function message takes the same params object.

### `viewer`

| Key                                   | English                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `viewer.document`                     | Document                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `viewer.loading`                      | Loading document…                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `viewer.openFailed`                   | This document could not be opened.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `viewer.pageFailed` (function)        | Page {page} could not be shown.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `viewer.saveFailed`                   | Your changes could not be written into this file.                                                                                                                                          |
| `viewer.saveUnavailable`              | Saving is not available right now. Check your connection and try again.                                                                                                                    |
| `viewer.preparingFile`                | Preparing your file…                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `viewer.applyRedactions`              | Apply redactions                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `viewer.redactTitle`                  | Apply redactions?                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `viewer.redactSummary` (function)     | This removes the content under {marks, plural, one {{marks} mark} other {{marks} marks}} on {pages, plural, one {{pages} page} other {{pages} pages}}.                                     |
| `viewer.redactLocked` (function)      | one: {count} mark saved in this file earlier will be applied too. \| other: {count} marks saved in this file earlier will be applied too.                                                  |
| `viewer.redactPermanent`              | It cannot be undone.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `viewer.redactOverlapped` (function)  | one: {count} other annotation under the marks will be removed too. \| other: {count} other annotations under the marks will be removed too.                                                |
| `viewer.redactSigned`                 | This file is signed. Its signature will stop verifying.                                                                                                                                    |
| `viewer.redactConfirm`                | Apply                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `viewer.redactCancel`                 | Cancel                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `viewer.redacting`                    | Applying redactions…                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `viewer.redactFailed`                 | The redactions could not be applied. Nothing was changed.                                                                                                                                  |
| `viewer.redactUnremovable` (function) | one: {count} mark covers content that cannot be removed. Move or delete it and try again. \| other: {count} marks cover content that cannot be removed. Move or delete them and try again. |
| `viewer.redactUnverified`             | Some content could not be removed, so nothing was changed.                                                                                                                                 |
| `viewer.redactUnavailable`            | Redaction is not available right now. Check your connection and try again.                                                                                                                 |

| `viewer.redactHiddenLayers`           | This file has hidden layers. Their content was not removed.                                                                                                                                |
| `viewer.redactForeign` (function)     | one: {count} redaction mark from another program was left in place. \| other: {count} redaction marks from another program were left in place.                                             |

# Vue

> Use Inkbar in a Vue 3 app with components and composables.

Vue 3 components and composables for Inkbar. The components are unstyled primitives built on `@inkbar/core`.

Install the packages as the [Quickstart](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/quickstart/) shows.

Vue 3.5 or later is a peer dependency. Add the Vite plugin from `@inkbar/core/vite` so PDF.js can load its worker and fonts; [Loading assets](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/loading-assets/) covers it.

## Usage

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  InkRoot,
  InkViewport,
  InkToolbar,
  InkToolButton,
  InkToolbarSeparator,
  InkUndo,
  InkRedo,
  InkPrevPage,
  InkPageInput,
  InkPageCount,
  InkNextPage,
  InkZoomSelect,
  InkThreadPopover,
} from '@inkbar/vue'
import { highlightTool, noteTool, redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
import type { Annotation } from '@inkbar/core'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


defineProps<{ signedUrl: string; documentId: string }>()


const annotations = ref<Annotation[]>([])
const tools = [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()]
</script>


<template>
  <InkRoot
    :src="{ url: signedUrl, key: documentId }"
    :assets="assets"
    :tools="tools"
    v-model:annotations="annotations"
  >
    <InkToolbar>
      <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
      <InkToolButton tool="select" />
      <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
      <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
      <InkToolButton tool="note" />
      <InkToolbarSeparator />
      <InkUndo />
      <InkRedo />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkViewport />
    <InkToolbar label="Page and zoom">
      <InkPrevPage />
      <InkPageInput />
      <InkPageCount />
      <InkNextPage />
      <InkZoomSelect />
    </InkToolbar>
    <InkThreadPopover />
  </InkRoot>
</template>
```

`select-text` and `select` are always there. Every other tool is opt-in: pass the ones you offer through `tools`, from the tool factories in `@inkbar/core/dom`, or `allTools()` for all of them. A button for a tool you did not pass renders disabled and hidden, a tool menu renders nothing, and each logs an `InkError('UnknownTool')` to the console once. If the active tool leaves `tools`, the viewer switches to `select-text` and reports it through `update:tool`.

Each control is a separate component, so put them in any order or leave some out. Buttons show icons from `@inkbar/icons`. Put your own in a button’s default slot to replace one, and use `InkIcon` to put the same icons on your own buttons. For a button of your own, such as `<InkToolbarButton @click="download">Download</InkToolbarButton>`, use `InkToolbarButton`: it joins the toolbar’s arrow-key focus and looks like the other buttons. [Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/) lists every control.

`v-model:annotations` makes your list the source of truth. Leave it off and Inkbar keeps the state itself, with undo and redo.

`InkViewport` zooms the document on a two-finger pinch, a trackpad pinch or ctrl+wheel. With `:pinch-zoom="false"`, the browser handles pinches and zooms the whole page.

## Forms

`InkViewport` fills the PDF’s form fields and runs the form’s scripts. `useForm()` returns the fields, their values, and `set` and `reset`. Bind `v-model:fields` to hold the values in your own state. The form never submits, opens a link, sends mail or prints: `@action` hands each request to you. `:form-highlight="false"` turns off the field tint, and a change applies to the open document in place.

[Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/) covers controlled fields, form actions, scripts, signature fields and saving values as Gloss.

## Signatures

`InkSignatureMenu` lists the saved signatures, turns on the `signature` tool with the chosen one, and opens `InkSignatureDialog` to draw, type or upload a new one. The menu needs `signatureTool()` in `tools`. The dialog and signature form fields work without it; the dialog then only saves the signature. These are marks on the page, not cryptographic signatures. `InkRoot` keeps them in its [`storage`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/): `createLocalStorage(prefix)` from `@inkbar/core` uses `localStorage`, and the default store forgets them on reload. `signatureFonts` lists the handwriting fonts the Type tab offers. Load them with `@font-face`. [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/) has the details.

## Thread popover

`InkThreadPopover` opens the thread of the activated note or text markup. A new note or highlight has no text yet, so the form first writes its own text (labelled “Comment”); after that it adds replies.

A root note with no text and no replies is removed when its popover closes, or when activation moves to another annotation, so abandoned notes do not stay on the page. Locked notes are never removed. If you add notes yourself (`add({ type: 'note', ... })`), give them `contents`, or they will be removed the first time someone opens and closes them.

## Custom rendering

Slots let you render parts yourself. `InkViewport` has `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `locked`, `annotation` and `page-error` slots. `InkThreadPopover` has a scoped default slot that receives the popover’s props, the default slot of `InkToolButton` receives `{ active, label }`, and that of `InkCommand` receives `{ label, busy }`. The props are typed as `AnnotationSlotProps` and `ThreadPopoverSlotProps`, the same types the React and Svelte packages export.

`InkRoot` takes `decorate-annotation`, a function that returns your own `data`, `classes` and `description` for an annotation’s element, as `mountViewer` describes in [Your own chrome](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#your-own-chrome). Pass a new function when its output depends on your own state, and Inkbar applies it again.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { DecorateAnnotation } from '@inkbar/vue'


const decorate: DecorateAnnotation = (a) =>
  a.custom?.review === 'open'
    ? { data: { review: 'open' }, description: 'Needs review' }
    : undefined
</script>


<template>
  <InkRoot :src="file" :assets="assets" :decorate-annotation="decorate">
    <InkViewport />
  </InkRoot>
</template>
```

For your own card next to an annotation, read the `activated` and `rootEl` refs and `setActivated` from `injectInkContext()` and use them with `createFocusReturn` and `createPopover`, as [Your own popovers](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#your-own-popovers) shows. The context’s `setActivated` emits `activate` for an id; `viewer.setActivated` in plain DOM does not.

`InkRoot`, `InkToolbar`, `InkToolButton`, `InkToolbarButton`, `InkCommand`, `InkUndo`, `InkRedo`, `InkPrevPage`, `InkNextPage`, `InkZoomIn` and `InkZoomOut` take `as-child` to render your own element in place of theirs, such as a button from your design system. Put that element in the default slot. The control keeps its behaviour and accessible name.

## Plugins

Pass plugins to `InkRoot` as `:plugins`. The list is read once, when the root mounts. A plugin’s tools join the viewer’s on their own, without `tools`. Nothing a plugin adds shows until you place it: a command with `InkCommand id="<plugin>.<id>"`, a tool with `InkToolButton tool="<plugin>.<id>"`. For a control of your own, `useCommand(id)` returns the command’s `run`, `enabled`, `busy`, `status`, `label` and `icon`. [Plugins](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/plugins/) covers placing commands, saving plugin records and undo, and [Writing a plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/) covers building one.

## Translations

`InkRoot` takes `messages` and `locale`. Pass a set such as `fr` from `@inkbar/core/locales/fr`, or a partial one to change a few strings. Changing either relabels the viewer in place. Labels you pass, such as `label` on `InkPanel` or `InkToolButton`, take a string or a function. See [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/).

## Keyboard

The scroll area takes focus. From there:

* With the `highlight` or `redact-area` tool active, `Enter` turns the text selection into a mark.
* With the `note` tool active, `Enter` places a note at the centre of the current page and opens it.

On a focused annotation:

* `Enter` or `Space` selects and activates it. A note or text markup opens its thread; other types are only selected.
* `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` move to the previous or next annotation on the page.
* `Shift` + arrow moves it by 1 pt, or by 10 pt with `Alt` as well.
* `Ctrl` or `Cmd` + `Shift` + arrow resizes an area redaction, text box or shape.
* `Delete` or `Backspace` removes it.

The full table, with the zoom and page keys, is in [Annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#tools-and-keyboard).

## Styling

Components carry state on data attributes, for example `[data-annotation][data-state="selected"]` and `[data-tool="highlight"][data-state="on"]`. `@inkbar/theme` gives a default look. Your own CSS overrides it without `!important`. An annotation’s shape, colours and text come from its data, and a stylesheet cannot repaint them.

## Composables

`useDocument`, `useAnnotations`, `useTool`, `useSelection`, `useZoom`, `usePage`, `useHistory`, `useEmbedded`, `useCommand`, `useSearch`, `useForm`, `useToolOptions`, `useToolStyle`, `useRecords` and `useRecordSelection` read the state of the nearest `InkRoot`. Build your own controls or side panel from them. [Lists of records](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/#lists-of-records) covers `useRecords` and `useRecordSelection`.

`useReadable(source, fallback)` follows any core readable, passed as is, as a ref or as a getter. It returns a read-only ref that holds `fallback` while there is none.

# React

> Use Inkbar in a React 19 app with components and hooks.

React components and hooks for Inkbar. The components are unstyled primitives built on `@inkbar/core`.

Install the packages as the [Quickstart](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/quickstart/) shows.

React 19 and React DOM 19 are peer dependencies. Add the Vite plugin from `@inkbar/core/vite` so PDF.js can load its worker and fonts; [Loading assets](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/loading-assets/) covers it. The package is marked `'use client'`, so a React Server Components app can import it from a server component.

## Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import {
  InkRoot,
  InkViewport,
  InkToolbar,
  InkToolButton,
  InkToolbarSeparator,
  InkUndo,
  InkRedo,
  InkPrevPage,
  InkPageInput,
  InkPageCount,
  InkNextPage,
  InkZoomSelect,
  InkThreadPopover,
} from '@inkbar/react'
import { highlightTool, noteTool, redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
import type { Annotation } from '@inkbar/core'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


const tools = [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()]


export function Review({
  signedUrl,
  documentId,
}: {
  signedUrl: string
  documentId: string
}) {
  const [annotations, setAnnotations] = useState<Annotation[]>([])
  return (
    <InkRoot
      src={{ url: signedUrl, key: documentId }}
      assets={assets}
      tools={tools}
      annotations={annotations}
      onAnnotationsChange={setAnnotations}
    >
      <InkToolbar>
        <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
        <InkToolButton tool="select" />
        <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
        <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
        <InkToolButton tool="note" />
        <InkToolbarSeparator />
        <InkUndo />
        <InkRedo />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkViewport />
      <InkToolbar label="Page and zoom">
        <InkPrevPage />
        <InkPageInput />
        <InkPageCount />
        <InkNextPage />
        <InkZoomSelect />
      </InkToolbar>
      <InkThreadPopover />
    </InkRoot>
  )
}
```

`select-text` and `select` are always there. Every other tool is opt-in: pass the ones you offer through `tools`, from the tool factories in `@inkbar/core/dom`, or `allTools()` for all of them. A button for a tool you did not pass renders disabled and hidden, a tool menu renders nothing, and each logs an `InkError('UnknownTool')` to the console once. If the active tool leaves `tools`, the viewer switches to `select-text` and reports it through `onToolChange`.

Each control is a separate component, so put them in any order or leave some out. Buttons show icons from `@inkbar/icons`. Pass your own as `children` to replace one, and use `InkIcon` to put the same icons on your own buttons. For a button of your own, such as `<InkToolbarButton onClick={download}>Download</InkToolbarButton>`, use `InkToolbarButton`: it joins the toolbar’s arrow-key focus and looks like the other buttons. [Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/) lists every control.

`annotations` with `onAnnotationsChange` makes your list the source of truth. Leave them off and Inkbar keeps the state itself, with undo and redo.

`InkViewport` zooms the document on a two-finger pinch, a trackpad pinch or ctrl+wheel. With `pinchZoom={false}`, the browser handles pinches and zooms the whole page.

## Forms

`InkViewport` fills the PDF’s form fields and runs the form’s scripts. `useForm()` returns the fields, their values, and `set` and `reset`. Pass `fields` with `onFieldsChange` to hold the values in your own state. The form never submits, opens a link, sends mail or prints: `onAction` hands each request to you. `formHighlight={false}` turns off the field tint, and a change applies to the open document in place.

[Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/) covers controlled fields, form actions, scripts, signature fields and saving values as Gloss.

## Signatures

`InkSignatureMenu` lists the saved signatures, turns on the `signature` tool with the chosen one, and opens `InkSignatureDialog` to draw, type or upload a new one. The menu needs `signatureTool()` in `tools`. The dialog and signature form fields work without it; the dialog then only saves the signature. These are marks on the page, not cryptographic signatures. `InkRoot` keeps them in its [`storage`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/): `createLocalStorage(prefix)` from `@inkbar/core` uses `localStorage`, and the default store forgets them on reload. `signatureFonts` lists the handwriting fonts the Type tab offers. Load them with `@font-face`. [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/) has the details.

## Thread popover

`InkThreadPopover` opens the thread of the activated note or text markup. A new note or highlight has no text yet, so the form first writes its own text (labelled “Comment”); after that it adds replies.

A root note with no text and no replies is removed when its popover closes, or when activation moves to another annotation, so abandoned notes do not stay on the page. Locked notes are never removed. If you add notes yourself (`add({ type: 'note', ... })`), give them `contents`, or they will be removed the first time someone opens and closes them.

## Custom rendering

Slots are render props. `InkViewport` takes `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `locked`, `renderAnnotation` and `renderPageError`; `InkThreadPopover` takes a function as `children`; `InkToolButton` takes a node or a function of `{ active, label }`; `InkCommand` a node or a function of `{ label, busy }`. The props each receives are typed as `AnnotationSlotProps` and `ThreadPopoverSlotProps`, the same types the Vue and Svelte packages export.

`InkRoot` takes `decorateAnnotation`, which returns your own `data`, `classes` and `description` for an annotation’s element, as `mountViewer` describes in [Your own chrome](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#your-own-chrome). Pass a new function when its output depends on your own state, and Inkbar applies it on the next render.

```tsx
import type { DecorateAnnotation } from '@inkbar/react'


const decorate: DecorateAnnotation = (a) =>
  a.custom?.review === 'open' ? { data: { review: 'open' }, description: 'Needs review' } : undefined


<InkRoot src={file} assets={assets} decorateAnnotation={decorate}>
  <InkViewport />
</InkRoot>
```

For your own card next to an annotation, read `activated`, `setActivated` and `rootEl` from `useInkContext` and use them with `createFocusReturn` and `createPopover`, as [Your own popovers](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#your-own-popovers) shows. The context’s `setActivated` calls `onActivate` for an id; `viewer.setActivated` in plain DOM does not.

`InkRoot`, `InkToolbar`, `InkToolButton`, `InkToolbarButton`, `InkCommand`, `InkUndo`, `InkRedo`, `InkPrevPage`, `InkNextPage`, `InkZoomIn` and `InkZoomOut` take `asChild` to render your own element in place of theirs, such as a button from your design system. Pass that element as the only child. The control keeps its behaviour and accessible name.

## Plugins

Pass plugins to `InkRoot` as `plugins`. The list is read once, when the root mounts. A plugin’s tools join the viewer’s on their own, without `tools`. Nothing a plugin adds shows until you place it: a command with `InkCommand id="<plugin>.<id>"`, a tool with `InkToolButton tool="<plugin>.<id>"`. For a control of your own, `useCommand(id)` returns the command’s `run`, `enabled`, `busy`, `status`, `label` and `icon`. [Plugins](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/plugins/) covers placing commands, saving plugin records and undo, and [Writing a plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/) covers building one.

## Translations

`InkRoot` takes `messages` and `locale`. Pass a set such as `fr` from `@inkbar/core/locales/fr`, or a partial one to change a few strings. Changing either relabels the viewer in place. Labels you pass, such as `label` on `InkPanel` or `InkToolButton`, take a string or a function. See [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/).

## Keyboard

The scroll area takes focus. From there:

* With the `highlight` or `redact-area` tool active, `Enter` turns the text selection into a mark.
* With the `note` tool active, `Enter` places a note at the centre of the current page and opens it.

On a focused annotation:

* `Enter` or `Space` selects and activates it. A note or text markup opens its thread; other types are only selected.
* `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` move to the previous or next annotation on the page.
* `Shift` + arrow moves it by 1 pt, or by 10 pt with `Alt` as well.
* `Ctrl` or `Cmd` + `Shift` + arrow resizes an area redaction, text box or shape.
* `Delete` or `Backspace` removes it.

The full table, with the zoom and page keys, is in [Annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#tools-and-keyboard).

## Styling

Components carry state on data attributes, for example `[data-annotation][data-state="selected"]` and `[data-tool="highlight"][data-state="on"]`. `@inkbar/theme` gives a default look. Your own CSS overrides it without `!important`. An annotation’s shape, colours and text come from its data, and a stylesheet cannot repaint them. `InkRoot`, `InkViewport`, `InkToolbar` and the toolbar controls accept `className`.

## Hooks

`useDocument`, `useAnnotations`, `useTool`, `useSelection`, `useZoom`, `usePage`, `useHistory`, `useEmbedded`, `useCommand`, `useSearch`, `useForm`, `useToolOptions`, `useToolStyle`, `useRecords` and `useRecordSelection` read the state of the nearest `InkRoot`. Build your own controls or side panel from them. [Lists of records](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/#lists-of-records) covers `useRecords` and `useRecordSelection`.

`useReadable(readable, fallback)` follows any core readable and returns its value, or `fallback` while there is none. Keep `fallback` a stable reference, such as a module constant.

# Svelte

> Use Inkbar in a Svelte 5 app with components and hooks.

Svelte 5 components and hooks for Inkbar. The components are unstyled primitives built on `@inkbar/core`.

Install the packages as the [Quickstart](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/quickstart/) shows.

Svelte 5.46.4 or later is a peer dependency. Add the Vite plugin from `@inkbar/core/vite` so PDF.js can load its worker and fonts; [Loading assets](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/loading-assets/) covers it. The package ships `.svelte` sources, so your bundler compiles them for your target, including the server.

## Usage

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import {
    InkRoot,
    InkViewport,
    InkToolbar,
    InkToolButton,
    InkToolbarSeparator,
    InkUndo,
    InkRedo,
    InkPrevPage,
    InkPageInput,
    InkPageCount,
    InkNextPage,
    InkZoomSelect,
    InkThreadPopover,
  } from '@inkbar/svelte'
  import { highlightTool, noteTool, redactAreaTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'
  import type { Annotation } from '@inkbar/core'
  import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
  import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


  let { signedUrl, documentId }: { signedUrl: string; documentId: string } = $props()


  let annotations = $state.raw<Annotation[]>([])
  const tools = [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()]
</script>


<InkRoot src={{ url: signedUrl, key: documentId }} {assets} {tools} bind:annotations>
  <InkToolbar>
    <InkToolButton tool="select-text" />
    <InkToolButton tool="select" />
    <InkToolButton tool="highlight" />
    <InkToolButton tool="redact-area" />
    <InkToolButton tool="note" />
    <InkToolbarSeparator />
    <InkUndo />
    <InkRedo />
  </InkToolbar>
  <InkViewport />
  <InkToolbar label="Page and zoom">
    <InkPrevPage />
    <InkPageInput />
    <InkPageCount />
    <InkNextPage />
    <InkZoomSelect />
  </InkToolbar>
  <InkThreadPopover />
</InkRoot>
```

`select-text` and `select` are always there. Every other tool is opt-in: pass the ones you offer through `tools`, from the tool factories in `@inkbar/core/dom`, or `allTools()` for all of them. A button for a tool you did not pass renders disabled and hidden, a tool menu renders nothing, and each logs an `InkError('UnknownTool')` to the console once. If the active tool leaves `tools`, the viewer switches to `select-text` and reports it through `onToolChange`.

Each control is a separate component, so put them in any order or leave some out. Buttons show icons from `@inkbar/icons`. Pass your own as `children` to replace one, and use `InkIcon` to put the same icons on your own buttons. For a button of your own, such as `<InkToolbarButton onclick={download}>Download</InkToolbarButton>`, use `InkToolbarButton`: it joins the toolbar’s arrow-key focus and looks like the other buttons. [Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/) lists every control.

`bind:annotations` makes your list the source of truth. Declare it with `$state.raw`, since Inkbar replaces the list whole. Leave the binding off and Inkbar keeps the state itself, with undo and redo. [Controlled mode](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/controlled-mode/) covers the details.

`tool`, `page` and `zoom` are bindable too, and each has a callback prop such as `onToolChange` if you would rather not bind.

`InkViewport` zooms the document on a two-finger pinch, a trackpad pinch or ctrl+wheel. With `pinchZoom={false}`, the browser handles pinches and zooms the whole page.

## Forms

`InkViewport` fills the PDF’s form fields and runs the form’s scripts. `useForm()` returns the fields, their values, and `set` and `reset`. Use `bind:fields` to hold the values in your own state. The form never submits, opens a link, sends mail or prints: `onaction` hands each request to you. `formHighlight={false}` turns off the field tint, and a change applies to the open document in place.

[Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/) covers controlled fields, form actions, scripts, signature fields and saving values as Gloss.

## Signatures

`InkSignatureMenu` lists the saved signatures, turns on the `signature` tool with the chosen one, and opens `InkSignatureDialog` to draw, type or upload a new one. The menu needs `signatureTool()` in `tools`. The dialog and signature form fields work without it; the dialog then only saves the signature. These are marks on the page, not cryptographic signatures. `InkRoot` keeps them in its [`storage`](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/storage/): `createLocalStorage(prefix)` from `@inkbar/core` uses `localStorage`, and the default store forgets them on reload. `signatureFonts` lists the handwriting fonts the Type tab offers. Load them with `@font-face`. [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/) has the details.

## Thread popover

`InkThreadPopover` opens the thread of the activated note or text markup. A new note or highlight has no text yet, so the form first writes its own text (labelled “Comment”); after that it adds replies.

A root note with no text and no replies is removed when its popover closes, or when activation moves to another annotation, so abandoned notes do not stay on the page. Locked notes are never removed. If you add notes yourself (`add({ type: 'note', ... })`), give them `contents`, or they will be removed the first time someone opens and closes them.

## Custom rendering

Slots are snippets. `InkViewport` takes `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `locked`, `annotation` and `pageError`. `InkThreadPopover` takes `children` as a snippet that receives the popover’s props. `InkToolButton` takes `children` as a snippet of `{ active, label }`, and `InkCommand` one of `{ label, busy }`. The props each receives are typed as `AnnotationSlotProps` and `ThreadPopoverSlotProps`, the same types the Vue and React packages export.

`InkRoot` takes `decorateAnnotation`, which returns your own `data`, `classes` and `description` for an annotation’s element, as `mountViewer` describes in [Your own chrome](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#your-own-chrome). Pass a new function when its output depends on your own state, and Inkbar applies it again.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import type { DecorateAnnotation } from '@inkbar/svelte'


  const decorate: DecorateAnnotation = (a) =>
    a.custom?.review === 'open'
      ? { data: { review: 'open' }, description: 'Needs review' }
      : undefined
</script>


<InkRoot src={file} {assets} decorateAnnotation={decorate}>
  <InkViewport />
</InkRoot>
```

For your own card next to an annotation, read `activated`, `setActivated` and `rootEl` from `useInkContext` and use them with `createFocusReturn` and `createPopover`, as [Your own popovers](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/frameworks/plain-dom/#your-own-popovers) shows. The context’s `setActivated` calls `onActivate` for an id; `viewer.setActivated` in plain DOM does not.

`InkRoot`, `InkToolbar`, `InkToolButton`, `InkToolbarButton`, `InkCommand`, `InkUndo`, `InkRedo`, `InkPrevPage`, `InkNextPage`, `InkZoomIn` and `InkZoomOut` take a `child` snippet to render your own element. Spread the `props` it gives you on that element. The snippet type is exported as `ChildSnippet`.

```svelte
<InkToolbar>
  {#snippet child({ props })}
    <nav {...props} class="my-toolbar">…</nav>
  {/snippet}
</InkToolbar>
```

## Plugins

Pass plugins to `InkRoot` as `plugins`. The list is read once, when the root mounts. A plugin’s tools join the viewer’s on their own, without `tools`. Nothing a plugin adds shows until you place it: a command with `InkCommand id="<plugin>.<id>"`, a tool with `InkToolButton tool="<plugin>.<id>"`. For a control of your own, `useCommand(id)` returns the command’s `run`, `enabled`, `busy`, `status`, `label` and `icon`. [Plugins](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/plugins/) covers placing commands, saving plugin records and undo, and [Writing a plugin](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/writing-a-plugin/) covers building one.

## Translations

`InkRoot` takes `messages` and `locale`. Pass a set such as `fr` from `@inkbar/core/locales/fr`, or a partial one to change a few strings. Changing either relabels the viewer in place. Labels you pass, such as `label` on `InkPanel` or `InkToolButton`, take a string or a function. See [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/).

## Keyboard

The scroll area takes focus. From there:

* With the `highlight` or `redact-area` tool active, `Enter` turns the text selection into a mark.
* With the `note` tool active, `Enter` places a note at the centre of the current page and opens it.

On a focused annotation:

* `Enter` or `Space` selects and activates it. A note or text markup opens its thread; other types are only selected.
* `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` move to the previous or next annotation on the page.
* `Shift` + arrow moves it by 1 pt, or by 10 pt with `Alt` as well.
* `Ctrl` or `Cmd` + `Shift` + arrow resizes an area redaction, text box or shape.
* `Delete` or `Backspace` removes it.

The full table, with the zoom and page keys, is in [Annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/#tools-and-keyboard).

## Styling

Components carry state on data attributes, for example `[data-annotation][data-state="selected"]` and `[data-tool="highlight"][data-state="on"]`. `@inkbar/theme` gives a default look. Your own CSS overrides it without `!important`. An annotation’s shape, colours and text come from its data, and a stylesheet cannot repaint them. `InkRoot`, `InkViewport`, `InkToolbar` and the toolbar controls accept `class`.

## Hooks

`useDocument`, `useAnnotations`, `useTool`, `useSelection`, `useZoom`, `usePage`, `useHistory`, `useEmbedded`, `useCommand`, `useSearch`, `useForm`, `useToolOptions`, `useToolStyle`, `useRecords` and `useRecordSelection` read the state of the nearest `InkRoot`. Call them during component initialisation, as you would `getContext`. Build your own controls or side panel from them. [Lists of records](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/#lists-of-records) covers `useRecords` and `useRecordSelection`.

`useReadable(() => readable, fallback)` follows any core readable. It returns an object whose `current` holds the value, or `fallback` while there is none.

Each hook returns an object whose reactive members are getters. Read `useZoom().zoom` in your template or an effect and it tracks. Destructure it (`const { zoom } = useZoom()`) and you copy the value once, so keep the object and read through it.

# Plain DOM

> Use Inkbar without a framework package, with createViewer and its toolbar controls, or mountViewer for your own chrome.

`@inkbar/core` has these entry points:

* `@inkbar/core` holds the document model and annotation store. It is safe to import during server rendering.
* `@inkbar/core/dom` renders pages, text layers and annotation layers into the DOM.
* `@inkbar/core/vite` is a Vite plugin that serves the PDF.js assets.
* `@inkbar/core/locales/fr` and `@inkbar/core/locales/de` hold the French and German [translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/).

Install `@inkbar/core` and `@inkbar/theme`, and set up the assets as [Loading assets](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/loading-assets/) describes.

## The whole viewer

`createViewer` opens a document and renders it into an element, with a thread popover for notes and text markup. You build the toolbars from controls that use the same markup as the framework packages, so `@inkbar/theme` styles them.

A viewer registers only the `select-text` and `select` tools until you pass `tools`. Import the creation tools you offer from `@inkbar/core/dom`, or pass `allTools()` for all eight. [Choosing tools](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/#choosing-tools) lists them.

```ts
import {
  createViewer,
  highlightTool,
  redactAreaTool,
  noteTool,
  createToolbar,
  createToolButton,
  createToolbarSeparator,
  createUndo,
  createRedo,
  createPrevPage,
  createPageInput,
  createPageCount,
  createNextPage,
  createZoomSelect,
} from '@inkbar/core/dom'
import { assets } from 'virtual:inkbar-assets'
import '@inkbar/theme/theme.css'


const viewer = createViewer(el, {
  source: file,
  assets,
  zoom: 'fit-width',
  tools: [highlightTool(), redactAreaTool(), noteTool()],
})


const tools = createToolbar()
tools.append(
  createToolButton(viewer, 'select-text'),
  createToolButton(viewer, 'select'),
  createToolButton(viewer, 'highlight'),
  createToolButton(viewer, 'redact-area'),
  createToolButton(viewer, 'note'),
  createToolbarSeparator(),
  createUndo(viewer),
  createRedo(viewer)
)


const pages = createToolbar({ label: 'Page and zoom' })
pages.append(
  createPrevPage(viewer),
  createPageInput(viewer),
  createPageCount(viewer),
  createNextPage(viewer),
  createZoomSelect(viewer)
)


viewer.element.prepend(tools) // above the document
viewer.element.append(pages) // below it


viewer.open(otherFile) // destroys the current document; the latest call wins
viewer.open(lockedFile, { password }) // this password applies to this load only
viewer.destroy()
```

Each control disables itself while no document is ready and lives as long as its viewer. `createZoomIn` and `createZoomOut` are there too. `createToolButton` takes `{ label }` as a third argument to rename a tool. For a tool the viewer doesn’t have, `createToolButton` and the highlight, shape and signature menus log `InkError('UnknownTool')`. The button renders disabled and hidden, and the menus render nothing.

Buttons show an icon from `@inkbar/icons`; replace their children with your own icon and the accessible name stays. `createIcon` draws any `@inkbar/icons` icon for your own buttons.

`createToolbar` gives one Tab stop to all its buttons, with arrow keys between them. A button you append joins that order, so your own buttons need no wrapper. An input, select or textarea you add keeps its arrow keys and its own `tabindex`: it is a Tab stop unless you give it `tabindex="-1"`.

`createViewer` takes the [`mountViewer` options](#your-own-chrome) except `container` and `document`, plus `source` and `assets` (both required), `password`, `passwordPrompt`, `engine`, `messages`, `locale`, `defaults`, `history`, `annotations`, `fields`, `plugins`, `redactionConfirm`, `onRedacted`, `onReady` and `onError`. `engine` turns on [saving into the PDF](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/saving/) and [applying redactions](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/redaction/), which `redactionConfirm` and `onRedacted` go with. Set `threads` to `false` to leave threads out. `viewer.status`, `viewer.document`, `viewer.engine`, `viewer.viewport` and `viewer.tools` are readables; the last two change when the engine rebuilds. `viewer.setMessages(set)` and `viewer.setLocale(tag)` switch language without a remount, and `viewer.messages` is the set in use; see [Translations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/translations/). `viewer.activated` is a readable too: the id of the annotation the user last clicked or activated with Enter or Space, or `null`. `viewer.setActivated(id)` activates one from your code without calling `onActivate`. It ignores an id the document doesn’t have, and `setActivated(null)` clears it. A password you pass to `open` replaces the `createViewer` one for that load. A locked file opens a password dialog unless you pass `passwordPrompt: false`; see [Locked files](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/locked-files/).

`plugins` takes plugins from `definePlugin`, set up once for the viewer’s life. Their tools join the viewer’s without `tools`. Place a plugin command with `createCommandButton(viewer, 'review.suggest')` and a plugin tool with `createToolButton(viewer, 'review.box')`. `viewer.commands.get(id)` returns a command for a control of your own. [Plugins](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/plugins/) has the details.

`createSearchButton(viewer)` opens the find bar from `createFindBar(viewer)`, which you append to `[data-ink-viewport-root]`. `viewer.search` holds the search state and actions. [Search](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/search/) has the details.

`createShapeMenu`, `createLineStyleMenu`, `createColorMenu` and `createTextStyleMenu` add the drawing controls (the shape menu needs `shapeTool()` in `tools`), and `viewer.engine.get()?.toolStyle` reads and sets the style they show. [Drawing](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/drawing/) has the details.

The viewer fills the PDF’s form fields and runs the form’s scripts. `viewer.form` is a readable that holds the open document’s form, or `null` before one is ready. `onAction` receives each submit, link, mail and print request, since the form never acts on them itself. `formHighlight: false` turns off the field tint, and `viewer.setFormHighlight(on)` changes it later. [Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/) has the details.

`createSignatureMenu(viewer)` lists the saved signatures and turns on the `signature` tool with the chosen one. It needs `signatureTool()` in `tools`. The signature dialog and signature form fields work without it; the dialog then only saves the signature. Pass `storage` and `signatureFonts` to `createViewer` to say where templates live and which handwriting fonts the dialog offers. [Signatures](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/signatures/) has the details.

`createViewer` reads the theme’s colours from the element you pass, so that element needs to be in the page when you call it. Like the framework packages, the viewer fills its parent, so give the element a height.

## Your own chrome

`mountViewer` wires the viewport, page layers, tools, and zoom and page keys onto a scroll container. You render everything around it.

```ts
import { openDocument } from '@inkbar/core'
import { mountViewer, highlightTool } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


const doc = await openDocument(file, { assets })
await doc.ready


const engine = mountViewer({
  container, // a focusable, scrollable element
  document: doc,
  zoom: 'fit-width',
  tools: [highlightTool()],
  onPageError: (page, error) => console.warn(page, error),
})
engine.tools.set('highlight')
engine.viewport.setZoom(1.5)
engine.viewport.scrollToPage(4)
engine.rebuild({ gap: 32 }) // construction-only options; zoom, page, tool and scroll position carry over
engine.destroy()
```

Options:

* `container` and `document`, both required.
* `tools`: the creation tools to register, from `allTools()` or the factories in `@inkbar/core/dom`. `select-text` and `select` are always present.
* `zoom` (a number, `'fit-width'` or `'fit-page'`; default `'fit-width'`), `page`, `mode` (`'continuous'` or `'single'`), `rotation` (0, 90, 180 or 270) and `tool` set the starting view. Change them later through `engine.viewport` and `engine.tools`.
* `gap`, `buffer`, `pinchZoom` and `customAnnotations` are fixed for a build. Change them with `engine.rebuild`.
* `pinchZoom` (default `true`) zooms the document when two fingers pinch over the container, and on a trackpad pinch or ctrl+wheel. Set it to `false` to leave pinching to the browser, which then zooms the whole page.
* `decorateAnnotation(annotation)` returns your own `data`, `classes` and `description` for an annotation’s element, or `undefined`. `{ data: { 'my-flag': 'on' } }` writes `data-my-flag="on"`, and `description` becomes the element’s `aria-description`. Data keys are lower-case kebab case. Inkbar applies them again whenever the annotations change. Call `engine.redecorate()` when they depend on anything else. Core’s own attributes and `ink-` classes always win.
* `onActivate(id)` fires when the user activates an annotation.
* `onBuild(viewport, tools)` fires after every build, the first one included, before `mountViewer` returns. Subscribe to the new viewport and tool controller here.
* `onPageMount(page, mount, host)` and `onPageUnmount(page)` fire as pages enter and leave the mounted range.
* `onPageError(page, error)` reports a page whose canvas or text layer failed, and `onPageError(page, null)` once every failed layer renders again. Unmounting a failed page emits no `null`, so clear any per-page error in `onPageUnmount`.

The viewport mounts pages synchronously, so a build’s page callbacks fire before its `onBuild`. During a rebuild, `engine.viewport` and `engine.tools` still point at the destroyed objects while those callbacks run. Read the arguments instead, or wait for `onBuild`.

## Your own popovers

`decorateAnnotation` tags your marks, and `createPopover` opens your own card next to one. The panel goes on `<body>` with `role="dialog"` and `data-ink-popover`, so `@inkbar/theme` gives it the viewer’s colour tokens. It follows the annotation’s element as pages mount and unmount, hiding while the page is gone. Tab stays inside the panel. Escape pressed in the panel or the viewer calls your `onDismiss`, as does a press outside the panel. A press on another annotation hands over to it instead.

```ts
import { createFocusReturn, createPopover, createViewer } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


const viewer = createViewer(el, {
  source: file,
  assets,
  decorateAnnotation: (a) =>
    a.custom?.review === 'open'
      ? { data: { review: 'open' }, description: 'Needs review' }
      : undefined,
})
const root = viewer.element // the [data-ink-root] element


const focusReturn = createFocusReturn({
  root: () => root,
  activated: () => viewer.activated.get(),
})
const card = createPopover({
  root,
  attrs: { class: 'review-card', 'aria-label': 'Review' },
  focusReturn,
  onDismiss: () => viewer.setActivated(null),
})


viewer.activated.subscribe((id) => {
  const a = id ? viewer.document.get()?.annotations.get(id) : undefined
  if (a?.custom?.review !== 'open') return card.hide()
  card.panel.textContent = a.contents ?? 'No comment'
  card.show(a.id)
})
```

Style the marks from the attributes you set, for example `[data-annotation][data-review="open"]`.

* `createFocusReturn({ root, activated })` decides where focus goes when the panel hides: back to the annotation, or to the next one on the page when you removed it. Call `focusReturn.beforeRemove(card.anchor)` just before you remove the anchored annotation. Its optional second argument is a selector, such as `'[data-review]'`, that sends focus to the next of your own marks first.
* `card.anchor` is the anchored annotation’s element, or `null` while its page is unmounted. `card.destroy()` removes the panel and its listeners.
* `placePanel(panel, rect)` positions a fixed panel below a `DOMRect`, or above it when only that fits, inside the window. Use it for a panel anchored to something other than an annotation.
* `observeAnnotationElement(root, id, onChange)` calls `onChange` with the element for annotation `id` now and whenever it changes, and returns a function that stops observing. `createPopover` uses it to follow the anchor.

A plugin’s marks and cards are built on these APIs. For a complete example, see the sandbox’s [suggestions plugin](https://github.com/inkbar/inkbar/blob/main/apps/sandbox/src/plugin/suggestions.ts). It keeps its own data under `custom.sandbox`.

## The document model on its own

`openDocument` works without any DOM, for example to read annotations or page text:

```ts
import { openDocument } from '@inkbar/core'


const doc = await openDocument(file, { assets })
await doc.ready


doc.annotations.add({ type: 'highlight', page: 0, quads })
const json = doc.exportAnnotations('json')
```

[Annotations](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/annotations/) covers the store, saving and the keyboard.

# Gloss format

> Inkbar exports and imports annotations as Gloss, an open JSON format for PDF annotations. What Inkbar adds to Gloss, what it leaves out, and how to validate an export.

`exportAnnotations` writes a [Gloss](https://gloss-format.org) document, and `importAnnotations` reads one. Gloss is an open JSON format for PDF annotations, with the same annotation types and coordinates as XFDF. The [Gloss docs](https://gloss-format.org) describe every field. This page covers what Inkbar does on top of them.

```json
{
  "format": "gloss",
  "version": 1,
  "documentKey": "contract-2026-10.pdf",
  "annotations": []
}
```

`documentKey` is the `doc.key` of the document the annotations belong to.

## Validate in your backend

Validate against the JSON Schema at `https://gloss-format.org/schema/v1.json`, or install the package, which ships the same schema with zod schemas and TypeScript types:

```sh
npm install gloss-format
```

Serve and accept the document as `application/vnd.gloss.annotations+json`.

Gloss accepts more than Inkbar imports. A document that validates against Gloss is well formed, but Inkbar can still turn an item away, as the next section explains.

## What Inkbar adds or leaves out

* **Embedded annotations stay in the file.** Annotations that came from the PDF never appear in an export.
* **Viewer state stays out.** In memory, every annotation carries `source` (`session` or `pdf`), and embedded ones carry `locked` and `hasAppearance`. The export drops them, and import ignores them.
* **Import is stricter than Gloss.** Every annotation needs `rect`, `color`, `opacity`, `createdAt` and `modifiedAt`, a free-text box needs `defaultStyle` with its `color`, and a redaction needs `interiorColor`. Gloss leaves these optional. An item without them comes back in the result’s `errors`, and the rest of the document still imports. Inkbar’s own exports always include them.
* **Unknown fields are dropped.** On a type Inkbar knows, import keeps the fields Gloss defines and drops the rest. Put your own data in `custom`, which Inkbar keeps as it is, apart from [`custom.inkbar`](#what-inkbar-writes-under-custominkbar).
* **Unknown types are kept.** An item with a type Inkbar doesn’t know, a string `id` and a numeric `page` comes back in the result’s `unknown` list, and the next export writes it out unchanged. Pass `unknown` to `exportAnnotations` yourself when you call it on a store directly.
* **PDF names are open.** A line ending, note icon or intent Inkbar doesn’t know loads and is written back unchanged. Inkbar draws a line ending it doesn’t know as `None`.
* **The speech bubble is a callout.** Inkbar’s speech bubble is a Gloss free-text callout with `cornerRadius` in points. Inkbar draws it as one rounded outline with a wedge to the tip. Other viewers ignore `cornerRadius` and draw a box with a leader line.

## What Inkbar writes under `custom.inkbar`

Gloss has no loupe, mask, pen pressure or free-text border colour, so Inkbar writes them under `custom.inkbar`. It writes a loupe as a circle and a mask as a circle or square, so other Gloss readers can still draw them. In Inkbar’s API they keep their plain names: the `loupe` and `mask` types, `pressure` and `borderColor`.

| In Inkbar                                                  | In the Gloss file                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ink` with `pressure`                                      | `custom.inkbar.pressure`                                                                                        |
| `freetext` with `borderColor`                              | `custom.inkbar.borderColor`                                                                                     |
| `loupe` with `rect`, `color`, `width`, `magnification`     | `type: "circle"` with `rect`, `color` and `width`, and `custom.inkbar: { "type": "loupe", "magnification": 2 }` |
| `mask` with `shape: "ellipse"` or `"rect"`, `color`, `dim` | `type: "circle"` or `"square"` with `color`, and `custom.inkbar: { "type": "mask", "dim": 0.5 }`                |

A loupe draws the page under its centre `magnification` times larger, inside a circle inscribed in `rect`. `color` and `width` give its rim. A mask dims the page outside its circle or square by `dim`, from 0 to 1, in `color`. A page holds one mask, and adding a second replaces the first.

This mask leaves an ellipse clear:

```json
{
  "type": "circle",
  "id": "0199c1a2-7e3b-7c00-8a11-5d2f4b6e9a10",
  "page": 0,
  "rect": { "x": 72, "y": 400, "width": 300, "height": 200 },
  "color": "#000000",
  "opacity": 1,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-19T12:00:00Z",
  "modifiedAt": "2026-10-19T12:00:00Z",
  "custom": { "inkbar": { "type": "mask", "dim": 0.7 } }
}
```

Inkbar merges its keys into any `custom.inkbar` already on the item, and leaves the rest of `custom` alone. On import it reads back only the keys it wrote. A circle or square without a `custom.inkbar.type` of `loupe` or `mask` stays a plain shape.

# Theme tokens

> The shadcn-compatible tokens and the annotation colour variables that Inkbar's stylesheet reads.

The stylesheet is compatible with shadcn token names. It reads these when your page defines them, and uses its own values when it does not:

* `--background`
* `--foreground`
* `--muted`
* `--muted-foreground`
* `--border`
* `--primary`
* `--primary-foreground`
* `--ring`
* `--radius`

Dark values apply under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` or inside a `.dark` ancestor. Add `.light` to the root or an ancestor to keep the light values, including inside a `.dark` ancestor.

Colour tokens must hold complete CSS colour values. Tokens written as bare HSL channels (`--muted: 210 40% 96%`) do not work. Write the full colour instead:

```css
--muted: hsl(210 40% 96%);
```

## Interface tokens

The stylesheet maps those names onto its own tokens. Set these on `[data-ink-root]` to style Inkbar without touching the rest of your page:

| Variable               | Reads                  | Used for                                          |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ink-bg`             | `--muted`              | The area around the pages and status messages     |
| `--ink-fg`             | `--foreground`         | Text                                              |
| `--ink-muted-fg`       | `--muted-foreground`   | Secondary text                                    |
| `--ink-surface`        | `--background`         | Toolbar, popovers, cards and resize handles       |
| `--ink-border`         | `--border`             | Borders                                           |
| `--ink-accent`         | `--primary`            | Active tools, selection boxes and primary buttons |
| `--ink-accent-fg`      | `--primary-foreground` | Text on the accent colour                         |
| `--ink-ring`           | `--ring`               | Focus rings                                       |
| `--ink-radius`         | `--radius`             | Corner radius                                     |
| `--ink-page-shadow`    |                        | The shadow under each page                        |
| `--ink-text-selection` |                        | Text selection on the page                        |

Some parts can render outside the root, so they read the same tokens from their own element: the thread popover from `[data-ink-thread-popover]`, a panel made by `createPopover` from `[data-ink-popover]`, the zoom select’s list from `[data-ink-select-content]`, the signature and password dialogs from `[data-ink-signature-dialog]` and `[data-ink-password-dialog]`, and form alerts from `[data-ink-form-alert]`. Sidebars read them from `[data-ink-sidebar]` too.

## Control sizes

Set these on an `InkToolbar`, or any ancestor, to size its controls:

| Variable             | Default    | Used for                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `--ink-control-size` | `2.25rem`  | Height of buttons, fields and the zoom select |
| `--ink-icon-size`    | `1.125rem` | Size of the icons inside them                 |

## Form fields

Set these on `[data-ink-root]` to style fillable fields:

| Variable                   | Used for                                       |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `--ink-form-field-bg`      | The tint on fillable fields                    |
| `--ink-form-field-focus`   | The focus ring and a signature field’s Sign    |
| `--ink-form-field-invalid` | The outline on a field whose value was refused |

Fields sit on the white page, so these change little in dark mode. To turn the tint off, pass `formHighlight: false`. See [Forms](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/forms/#theming).

## Outline and links

Set these on `[data-ink-root]`. See [Outline and links](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/outline-and-links/#theming):

| Variable                    | Used for                                 |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `--ink-outline-indent`      | The indent for each level of the outline |
| `--ink-outline-item-height` | The minimum height of an outline item    |
| `--ink-outline-current-bg`  | The tint behind the current outline item |
| `--ink-link-hover`          | The tint over a link under the pointer   |

## Sidebars, thumbnails and marks

| Variable                      | Default                         | Used for                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ink-sidebar-width`         | `320px`                         | The open sidebar’s width. The sidebar sets it on itself, so pass `defaultWidth` to change it. See [Sidebars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/sidebars/#in-css)                                      |
| `--ink-sidebar-rail-width`    | `48px`                          | The width of a sidebar’s rail                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--ink-thumbnail-width`       | Unset                           | A thumbnail’s width in px when you pass no `width`. A thumbnail list caps it at its own width less a 16px gutter on each side. Unset, a list fills its width and a single thumbnail is 120px wide |
| `--ink-thumbnail-shadow`      | A hairline edge and a soft lift | The shadow around thumbnails and search result cards                                                                                                                                              |
| `--ink-mark-selected-outline` | `2px solid #2740f5`             | The outline on the mark of a plugin record selected in a list, on the page or by your app                                                                                                         |

## Annotation colours

Set these variables on `[data-ink-root]` to change the default colour for new annotations:

| Variable                                                                  | Used for                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `--ink-highlight`, `--ink-underline`, `--ink-strikeout`, `--ink-squiggly` | Text markup                        |
| `--ink-note`                                                              | New notes                          |
| `--ink-free-text`                                                         | New text boxes (text colour)       |
| `--ink-shape`, `--ink-ink`                                                | Shapes, lines and freehand drawing |
| `--ink-redact`, `--ink-redact-fill`                                       | Redaction outline and fill         |

The theme declares these on `[data-ink-root]` itself, so a value on `:root` or another ancestor does not reach them. Target `[data-ink-root]`, or pass colours through the `defaults` option on `InkRoot` or `createViewer`.

Inkbar reads a colour when you create the annotation and stores it on the annotation. Changing a variable later affects new annotations only, and dark mode does not change annotation colours.

Inkbar draws an annotation from its data. A text box’s fill, border, corner radius, alignment and text style come from the annotation, and `--ink-free-text` sets only the text colour a new text box starts with. A note keeps its own colour whatever `--ink-note` says, and the theme adds a drop shadow to it on screen.

## Search highlights

Set these on `[data-ink-root]` to colour the matches of a [search](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/search/):

| Variable               | Used for          |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- |
| `--ink-search-hit`     | Every match       |
| `--ink-search-current` | The current match |

The theme draws the matches in a layer that multiplies with the page, so the text shows through the colour. Pages stay white in dark mode, so one pair of values serves both.

# Icons

> The 52 icons the toolbar controls show, which control shows each one, and how to use them on your own buttons.

The toolbar controls show icons from `@inkbar/icons`: 52 icons from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev), stored as plain data so the package has no dependencies.

* `TextCursor`Select text tool
* `SquareDashedMousePointer`Rectangle select tool
* `Highlighter`Highlight tool, and the highlight menu
* `Underline`Highlight menu, and the text style menu
* `Strikethrough`Highlight menu
* `SpellCheck2`Highlight menu, for squiggly
* `Square`Mark for redaction tool, and the rectangle shape
* `MessageSquare`Add note tool
* `MessageSquareText`Note icon on the page
* `Shapes`Shape tool
* `Slash`Line shape
* `MoveUpRight`Arrow shape
* `RectangleHorizontal`Rounded rectangle shape
* `Circle`Ellipse shape
* `MessageCircle`Speech bubble shape
* `Star`Star shape
* `Hexagon`Polygon shape
* `Search`Loupe shape, the Find button and search fields
* `SquareDashed`Mask shape
* `CircleDashed`Oval mask shape
* `Type`Text box tool
* `PenLine`Draw tool
* `PenTool`Sketch tool
* `Signature`Signature tool and menu
* `Trash2`Signature menu, to delete a saved signature
* `Plus`Signature menu, to add one, and Increase font size
* `Minus`Line style menu, and Decrease font size
* `ALargeSmall`Text style menu
* `Bold`Text style menu
* `Italic`Text style menu
* `AlignLeft`Text style menu
* `AlignCenter`Text style menu
* `AlignRight`Text style menu
* `AlignJustify`Text style menu
* `Undo2`Undo
* `Redo2`Redo
* `ZoomIn`Zoom in
* `ZoomOut`Zoom out
* `ChevronLeft`Previous page
* `ChevronRight`Next page
* `ArrowLeft`Back
* `ArrowRight`Forward
* `ChevronDown`Menu triggers, the zoom select, and Next match
* `ChevronUp`Previous match
* `CaseSensitive`Match case
* `X`Close find
* `Check`Beside the chosen colour, line style or zoom level
* `Download`Download
* `Printer`Print
* `MoveRight`No control: for your own buttons
* `List`No control: for your own buttons
* `Info`No control: for your own buttons

The core `createZoomSelect` is a native `<select>`. Inside a toolbar, the theme draws the `ChevronDown` shape on it in CSS, and it has no `Check`.

## Using an icon on your own button

The controls bring their icons with them. Install `@inkbar/icons` only when you want the same icons on your own buttons, so they match the rest of the toolbar:

```sh
pnpm add @inkbar/icons
```

Each framework package has an `InkIcon` component that draws one. Without a framework, `createIcon` from `@inkbar/core/dom` returns the `<svg>` element.

* Vue

  ```vue
  <script setup lang="ts">
  import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { InkIcon } from '@inkbar/vue'
  </script>


  <template>
    <button type="button" aria-label="Finish review">
      <InkIcon :icon="Check" />
    </button>
  </template>
  ```

* React

  ```tsx
  import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { InkIcon } from '@inkbar/react'


  export function FinishButton() {
    return (
      <button type="button" aria-label="Finish review">
        <InkIcon icon={Check} />
      </button>
    )
  }
  ```

* Svelte

  ```svelte
  <script lang="ts">
    import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
    import { InkIcon } from '@inkbar/svelte'
  </script>


  <button type="button" aria-label="Finish review">
    <InkIcon icon={Check} />
  </button>
  ```

* Plain DOM

  ```ts
  import { Check } from '@inkbar/icons'
  import { createIcon } from '@inkbar/core/dom'


  const finish = document.createElement('button')
  finish.type = 'button'
  finish.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Finish review')
  finish.append(createIcon(Check))
  ```

The icon is hidden from screen readers, so give the button its own name, as `aria-label` does here. `InkIcon` sets its width and height from `size`, which defaults to 18. With the theme loaded, CSS sizes every icon to `--ink-icon-size` (default `1.125rem`) instead, so set that variable on the button or an ancestor to change the size.

## Replacing a control’s icon

Give a control your own content and it shows that instead of its icon. Its accessible name stays the same. In Vue, use the default slot; in React and Svelte, pass `children`. A control from `@inkbar/core/dom` is an ordinary element, so replace its children: `undo.replaceChildren(yourSvg)`.

[Toolbars](/pr-preview/pr-52/docs/guides/toolbars/#icons-and-labels) has an example in each framework.

## Drawing an icon yourself

Each icon is an array of `[tag, attributes]` pairs. To draw one without `InkIcon` or `createIcon`, create each element inside an `<svg>` that has the attributes in `ICON_ATTRIBUTES`, plus a `width` and `height`.

## Licence

The icons come from Lucide under the ISC licence, and some of them derive from Feather under the MIT licence. The `@inkbar/icons` package carries both notices in its `LICENSE` file.
